Introduction
Sphere Ads (formerly Brand Awareness Ads) are designed to promote yourself and your services to take your advertising efforts to new heights and drive traffic to your website. The aim is to increase awareness of your brand in your community and drive brand recognition.
Summary
Sphere Ads (#h_01H9RSC9PVJB57EF9F9VX1S8CA)
Sphere Ad Creation (#h_01H9RSCXK3FSX5YZ1K09FV3J4H)
Campaign Tracking (#h_01H9RSD7FH674K39SKBJXD0345)
Sphere Ads
Lofty offers two (2) options for Sphere Ads, Basic Sphere Ads and Call Sphere Ads. Both options are
charged weekly
to promote you and your services to your community. Both ads are promoted on both Facebook and Instagram.
The only difference is, that Call Sphere Ads allow a potential lead to call you directly from your website, while Basic Sphere Ads provide the ad placement, without the option to call you directly.
The cost breakdown for each ad type is outlined below:
Basic Sphere Ads
Basic Sphere Ads start at $39 for one (1) week and can run for up to four (4) weeks. You will be billed the full amount upon purchase.
An example Basic Brand Ad:
Call Sphere Ads
Call Sphere Ads start at $69 for one (1) week and can run for up to four (4) weeks. You will be billed the full amount upon purchase.
An example is called a Brand Ad:
Sphere Ad Creation
The first step is to select Basic Sphere Ads or Call Sphere Ads and the duration of the ad will run, from 1-4 weeks. The required information is the same for both brand types.
Next, your profile information will be pre-loaded from your Lofty account information. Here, you can add a different photo, update your name and contact information, and select the location you want to target with these ads.
After submitting the payment, an ad preview will be available. Here, you can start customizing the advertisement.
Template
Click
Edit
under Template to change the ad template. Click on each template to see the preview update with your information. You can also upload your own image. Click
Save
once you have selected the template for the ad.
Ad Creative Settings
This section allows you to edit the contact information, photo, and content featured on the ad. Again, click
Save
to save the updates.
Location & Audience
This section allows you to set the location that these advertisements are targeting. Ideally, this is the area where you are hoping to gain business and establish your brand.
Note:
Only one (1) area can be selected.
Landing Page
This is the website that will open when a potential lead clicks on your ad. This can be your Lofty website, a Lofty Landing Page, or a Custom website.
Note:
If you select Custom Page, Lofty cannot track or monitor lead performance on the ad.
Lead Capture Setting
This section allows you to select the type of lead you want to attract whether the lead will be a team or private lead in the CRM, allows you to set lead routing rules, and will include a tag on the lead so they can be found easily.
Once you are satisfied with the advertisement settings, click
Publish
. Please note that once the ad has been published, the image content cannot be changed.
Campaign Tracking
Once the ad campaign has been published, the results can be tracked by navigating to
Marketing >  Brand Awareness > Sphere Ads.
Separate tabs are available to track Basic ads and Call ads. Click
+ New Sphere Ads
to create a new sphere ad campaign.
Note:
The campaign will be pending until the start date arrives.
Questions?

Introduction
The Property Tour tool allows Lofty users to create listing showing itineraries for potential home buyers and renters. This tool allows you to set the meeting time and location, as well as all the homes on the tour, and calculates the estimated travel time between each stop. If the lead has created a profile on your Lofty website, they are able to view the tour itinerary there and leave feedback for all of the homes they tour.
Summary
Setting up the Property Tour (#h_01GT2A14GE2XN52JYWRNQ3PW78)
From the Calendar (#h_01GT2A1DK9Y0KRCPM039M6F6T0)
From the Listings Page (#h_01GT2A1N1SZSVAS8Q2XPAZ2FB3)
From the Lead Profile (#h_01GT2A1TCH46YYP6RTSBD4AWR2)
Edit Property Tour (#01H8Q1TEVDH94MSM3NW9926ZNA)
The Lead Experience (#h_01GT2A202XRX1WB8QH2XCSNDC6)
Setting up the Property Tour
From the Calendar
Navigate to the Lofty calendar, click
+ Create,
and select
Add Property Tour
A pop-up will prompt you to select the lead that is taking the tour. Enter their information here to find the lead in the CRM.
Once the lead has been selected, you may start planning the tour. Click
Start Planning
to begin.
Click
Add Listing
to add homes to the property tour. Don't forget to also set a meeting location and time. If you need to change the order of the listings on the tour, click and hold the three-line icons to drag and drop the listings into their new order.
You can freely adjust the arrival time at each listing for more flexible planning. The tool will only prompt you when there is a time gap or overlap. Additionally, the refresh button has been enabled to recalculate the shortest time.
Click the three dots icon to contact the listing agent, view the listing details, or delete the listing from the tour.
By default, the tour will begin at 8 AM the following day. The tour will be added to your Lofty calendar, so please remember to schedule the correct time and date. The default time spent at each listing is 30 minutes, but can be as long as 2 hours. The tour will fail to generate if there are more than 10 listings on the tour and if the tour lasts longer than 24 hours.
Once the tour has been saved, you have the option to view the tour and email the tour to the lead. When sending the email, the template is pre-written and can be edited before sending. Be sure to click
Confirm
to save the tour.
From the Listings Page
Navigate to Listings and check the box next to at least one listing. Once the box is checked, click
Create Property Tour
to get started.
Next, the selected listings will be added to the tour and you will be prompted to select the lead for the tour.
Once the lead is selected, you have the opportunity to edit the tour. Again, remember to set your starting location, time, and date.
From the Lead Profile
Navigate to the lead's profile and select
Create Property Tour
from the menu in the three-dot icon.
Next, you may begin building the tour, the same as described above.
Edit Property Tour
When a property tour has been scheduled with a lead, the tour will be available in the Appointments section of the lead profile.
Click the
'...'
menu to see the Property Tour Options.
Click
Edit
to change the Property Tour. This will open the tour and you can rearrange the tour order, delete the listing from the tour, and add another listing to the tour.
The Lead Experience
If the lead has set up a profile on your Lofty website, they can view any scheduled and completed tours in the
My Tours & Showings
section of their account. The lead is also able to provide feedback on the listings they tour. This feedback will be available to view on the lead's profile in the Lofty CRM.

This feature allows you to set the schedule that Lofty users are available to accept phone calls.

.

phone
icon in the right side panel.
2. Click on the
more
menu to the left of the
Call List
and then toggle "Available" on/off.
Customize Working Hours
To customize working hours, do the following:
1. Open the Dialer Panel by clicking on the
phone
icon in the right side panel.
2. Click on the left panel option for the
Business Hours
option, and then set up your available working hours. The time zone should match your preferences. "Anytime" is the default option and will not limit availability for incoming phone calls. The option for "Customize working days/hours" will allow you to choose your schedule for each day to be available.
3. Click the blue "save" button
Manually Control Available/Unavailable on Mobile App
To manually control available/unavailable on the mobile app, do the following:
1.
Open the Dialer Panel by clicking on the "people" icon in the bottom menu, and then click Call List:
2. Click on the "more" option in the top-right:

Edit Working Hours from the Mobile App

2. Click on the "more" option in the top-right:

4. Adjust working hours:

Creating a Standard Call List
*Please note that depending on the package purchased, only a certain number of call lists can be active at one time:
Growth Call Package: Not applicable.
Elite Call Package: Maximum of 10 lists active at a time
Three Line Dialer Call Package: No maximum number of lists that can be active at a time
There are two ways to create a call list--both are outlined below.
Option 1: Select Leads and Import
Navigate to the
People
page, apply any filters needed, select the leads you want to add to the list, and select the "Send to Dialer" option.
New UI:
Old UI:
Only leads with valid phone numbers can be added to the list. Those listed as DNC or with invalid phone numbers will also be skipped.
Create your call list by clicking the "Create" button on the bottom-right of the call panel:
Option 2: Import Leads from the Call Panel
Open the call list panel and click the "+" button:
To import leads, first select from the available "Segments" or "Saved Filters" and then select a pipeline stage. Continue by clicking on the “Save & Next” button at the bottom right.
Just like before, only leads with valid phone numbers can be added to these lists. Others will be skipped during this import process.
Adjust Call List Settings
There are two important settings to adjust before starting to call a call list. Both of these settings can be found by clicking on the phone icon in the bottom-right, clicking on the drop-down menu at the top-left of that panel, and then clicking on
Settings
:
(1) Call List Dialing Preference
There are two different options here (a) and (b). They are outlined below.
(a) Dial all of a lead's phone numbers
. Select this option if you wish to contact a lead through any of their multiple contact numbers
AND
family member numbers. When dialing the call list, you can choose to call the Lead's next number or hang up and call the next lead instead.
If a lead answers, or sends your call to voice mail, you will be able to choose to continue calling other numbers by manually clicking on
Next Number
and choosing the number. If you would like to proceed with the next lead, click the
Finished
/
Next Lead
button instead.
(b) Dial a lead's primary phone number only
. This means that even if leads have multiple contact numbers on the lead profile, selecting this option will make it so that the call list will only call their primary phone number.
(2) Time Between Calls
Choose between 1, 3, 5, or 10 minutes between phone calls. This time is typically used to make notes, complete any follow-up work, etc.
Dialing the Call Lists
You can begin calling the list by clicking the green phone button on the Call List Page or, if you created the list but did not start calling, you can click on the phone icon in the bottom-right, and then select the list before choosing the green phone button.
If this is the first time you are calling this list, you will enter the menu for Start Calls - Call Settings. This menu allows you to control the following:
Use this phone number to call
. Choose the number you want to use to make the call.
Number of Lines to Dial
. This is only available if you have purchased the Three Line Dialer call package. See the
Three Line Dialer Guide (https://help.chime.me/hc/en-us/articles/360057685172)
for more information.
Seconds of the ring to determine the call as No Answer
. This is also a specific setting for the Three Line Dialer call package. See the
Three Line Dialer Guide (https://help.chime.me/hc/en-us/articles/360057685172)
for more information.
The Callback Message to Drop
. Another specific feature of the three-line dialer. See the
Three Line Dialer Guide (https://help.chime.me/hc/en-us/articles/360057685172)
for more information.
Call Script
. See
Call Scripts (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360000306052-Call-Scripts)
Questionnaire
. See
Call Questionnaires (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360000305632-Call-Questionnaires)
Auto Follow-Up Texts
. This text will be sent to every lead that is called right after the call ends--regardless of whether they answer the call or not.
Calling
During a Call
Incoming Call + Auto-Lead Record Opening
When an incoming call is received in Lofty, no page will auto-load and you must click on the lead's name in the top-right in order to navigate to their lead record which allows you to save any work before proceeding.
Call Result Pages
There are two types of call result pages. This is where you will select a call outcome, take notes, etc.
Type 1
This is the type that will appear if the lead you just called is
not
the last. From here you can choose from the following:
Click the pause button to pause this call list. You can resume at a later point in time.
Click the “Next Lead” button to end the current call and call the next lead. If you do not click this button, the system will call the next lead automatically after the indicated countdown expires.
Click the list button (bottom-right) to review the leads who have not been called yet.
Type 2
This type will appear if the person you just called was A.) the last lead on your list or B.) you chose to hang up the phone call and stop dialing down the list. From here you can choose from the following:
Click the “Finished” button to complete the call list.
If you do not click the "Finished" button, the system will automatically continue to dial after the time expires.
Call Report
After you finish the entire call list and click the “Finished” button on the call result page, you will be directed to the “Call Report” page. Here, you can check your call list preferences and archive this call list. Once a list is archived, you are
not
able to restore it.
Call List Details
Clicking on a list on the Call List page will take you to the Call List Detail Page. From h
ere you can check the call list data and outcomes as well as review any follow-up tasks that you have set.
Check the Call History
You can access the call history from the dialer menu. On this page, you can filter by "Type" or by "Date."
Reviewing Archived Lists
You can filter specific archived lists by the "Type" or "Date" filters and click the delete button to delete an archived call list. When you click on a list on the Archived List section you can also review the call list detail page as well.
FAQ
I tried creating a call script and got an error saying it "Count of call script Exceeded".
The call script error normally shows up if the CRM account is not using the correct package.
The call script is
only available for the Call Packages with the "Power Dialer" feature.
Questions?

#### Article 178: Calling Leads Best Practices

- Article ID: `360042818171`
- Category: `CRM`
- Section: `Calling`
- Updated: `2025-10-17T08:59:31Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360042818171-Calling-Leads-Best-Practices

Introduction
Calling your leads regularly will help you stay connected to your potential clients--especially if your local market is competitive. Assuming that your competition is also using email drip campaigns, property alerts, market reports, etc., then one of the best ways to stand out is to make sure you have a plan and a tool that you can use to call your leads on a regular basis to stay in contact and build relationships.
Summary
Deciding Who To Call (#h_01H0KCPR2ZJE6NZ894NX0P6K3K)
Deciding When To Call (#h_01H0KCPY7G3GKD3D7N595VNFBT)
Suggested Call Frequency (#h_01H0KCQ78WSKGVYFNPB9QZWJ9X)
Call Script Preparation (#h_01H0KCQD647E7N41856K6J5TPG)
Deciding
Who
To Call
Cold Calling / Prospecting Calling
If you have lead lists like FSBO or expired leads, make sure to import them into Lofty and then organize them by segments/tags (see
Lead Organization with Segments (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360038401831)
or
Lead Organization with Tags (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360038603951)
). You can use
Smart Call Lists (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360000314911)
or
Standard Call Lists (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360000305252)
to call these leads on a regular basis. Lofty also has a
Three Line Dialer (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360057685172)
that you can use to increase your calling efficiency! Click
here (https://chime.me/admin/home#/userbilling)
to add the Three Line Dialer now or click
here (https://chime.me/admin/home#/usersetting/manageDialer)
to upgrade your existing dialer seat.
Standard Call List (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360000305252)
functionality can be set up using Pipeline stages or Segments. For example, if you imported all FSBO/Expired Leads into Lofty and put them into the "New Leads" pipeline with the tag/segment of "FSBO" or "' Expired," then you can set up two standard call lists: one for Expired Leads and one for FSBO. Remember to give an exact name to the call list so that you can identify it easily.
Example of Segments:
Example of adding call lists based on Segments:
After creating these two call lists, you can start dialing by clicking the green call button.
When cold calling, you will likely come upon leads who ask you to never call them again. For these leads, remember to put them into a "DNC" (Do Not Contact) segment or pipeline stage while you are on the phone with them. This is easy to do because the lead profile will be populated on the left of the screen while you are calling each lead. You may also want to select their number and mark it as DNC as well (if applicable).
Alternatively, some of your leads may show high interest as buyers or sellers. Just remember to make any notes and move them into the applicable pipeline stage so that you can follow up with them appropriately. Remove them from the segment/pipeline stage that they were in when you started the cold calling to avoid calling them again with the same strategy.
Smart Call Lists (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360000314911)
are based on your Lofty tasks that are scheduled for today or are overdue. So, in order for these lists to be populated, you need to make sure you have tasks associated with leads either by adding them manually or by having a Smart Plan assigned that is doing this for you.
Using Expired Leads as an example, you could prepare a Smart Plan specifically for this type of lead (or consider using some of the built-in plans available in the library). More information on setting up a Smart Plan can be found here:
Smart Plans (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/7626737520923)
. If you want to do this quickly and easily, you could simply make the Smart Plan 1-3 call tasks. Make sure the tasks are indeed CALL tasks, otherwise, they will not trigger onto the Smart Call lists.
Be sure to also set up the triggering criteria so that the Smart Plan is auto-applied (if desired) or that you know how to manually apply it later on.
After tasks are associated with leads and due either today or are overdue, these leads will be added automatically to the Smart Call Lists that you can access regularly:
Nurturing Leads
If you have a "Nurturing" or a "Cold" pipeline stage in Lofty, you can use those criteria, plus other filters, to set up call lists as previously outlined in this and other linked articles. Reaching out to this type of lead is an important way to stay in contact. A powerful way of using Smart Plans is to mix in manual call tasks with automated emails/texts so that you can call now and again to stay top of mind.
Past Clients
Staying in touch with your past clients will help you get more referrals. With the same logic already explained, consider having a "Past Clients" pipeline stage so that you can call them regularly. Or, combine it with a Smart Plan to send out periodic emails and then trigger a task for you to call as well. Spending time calling past clients is a good investment of your time as long as it is timed correctly.
Deciding
When
To Call
One
Inman Study (https://www.inman.com/2012/05/07/agents-theres-gold-in-calling-cold/)
suggests that calling between 10:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m. yields the best results as far as connection rate is concerned. However, this depends on your area, your client preferences, and the specific individual you are calling. If you can, document the best times to call leads. Categorize your leads so that you know how to handle future calls and can easily access notes to remember any important details before making a phone call.  In the end, find what works best for you and your clients.
Suggested Call Frequency
The answer to how many calls you should make in one day depends on your goals and who you are calling. One
Inman study (https://www.inman.com/2012/05/07/agents-theres-gold-in-calling-cold/)
explained that it took 208 calls to get an appointment or referral. In other words, it could take about six hours to obtain one appointment. Set your goals for calling based on these basics. Also, keep in mind that you want to tailor your calls to your audience. Do not call leads that you already have a relationship with using the same strategy used for cold calling, etc.
With the
Lofty Three Line Dialer (https://help.chime.me/hc/en-us/articles/360042464691)
, you can easily call through long lists of leads in much less time than you would when dialing out with just one line. Click
here (https://chime.me/admin/home#/userbilling)
to add a new Three Line Dialer package or click
here (https://crm.lofty.com/admin/home#/usersetting/manageDialer?isShowNewDialer=true)
to upgrade your existing dialer package (*IMPORTANT: Only the Team Admin/Owner can buy or upgrade dialer seats)... (Only the team owners can buy or upgrade the dialer).
Call Script Preparation
You do not want to use a script if you are unable to make it sound natural. The key to not sounding robotic is practice, as you already know. Memorize the basics of the script and then practice until it sounds natural. You can always role-play with another agent, your spouse, children, etc.
Do not be afraid to change a script to make it more in tune with your personality and with how the lead responds.
Click here (https://theclose.com/real-estate-cold-calling-scripts/)
for just one source of cold-calling scripts that you may refer to. You can always search online for more scripts that you might find useful.
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at
<support@lofty.com (mailto:%3Csupport@chimeinc.com)
>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by a chat with us through your Lofty CRM.
Related terms: Lofty dialer, Call and text feature

#### Article 179: Inbound Call Forwarding

- Article ID: `360030644952`
- Category: `CRM`
- Section: `Calling`
- Updated: `2025-11-10T00:44:27Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360030644952-Inbound-Call-Forwarding

Introduction
Lofty provides a solution for making sure incoming phone calls are not missed. With this feature, incoming calls to Lofty virtual numbers will be forwarded to a specific phone number if the agent is not available or does not pick up the phone within a specified time.
*
This feature is available on all Lofty call packages.
Settings
The following is a screenshot of what the settings look like under
Settings
>
Call/Text> Info & Settings> Advanced Settings
:
Important Definitions
Bridge Number
: The number that is connected to the Lofty virtual number. For example, if you call a lead via click-to-call, the virtual number will call
this
number so you can answer, and then a call will be made to the person you are calling.
Forwarding Number
: This is the number that will be called when the bridge number is unavailable or the agent does not answer the call for the indicated time.
Transfer to Forwarding Number after
If a call is not answered within the defined time limit, the call will be transferred to the Transfer Number
.
This will also happen if the agent’s bridge number is busy, has no signal, etc. If the latter is the case, we will transfer the call immediately without waiting for the defined period.
Apply the rule to team members
: The switch is only available with “Manage Team” permission (see
Team Permissions (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360055290451)
). They can easily apply all the calls to the same phone number (maybe a company number) by this setting in case of changing the number of every account one by one.
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at
<support@lofty.com (mailto:%3Csupport@chimeinc.com)
>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

#### Article 180: Inbound Voicemail

- Article ID: `30358772627611`
- Category: `CRM`
- Section: `Calling`
- Updated: `2025-11-10T00:41:08Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/30358772627611-Inbound-Voicemail

Introduction
When a lead calls your Lofty virtual number, they have the option to leave a message on your voicemail box. This article shows you how to personalize your voicemail greeting message and check your messages.
Note:
When you configure your voicemail settings, these settings are on the personal level, not the phone number level. This means that if your lead calls you on either a personal virtual number or the company number, they will reach the same voicemail box.
Summary
Set up your Voicemail Greeting (#h_01JB095YHY4CGXQK4NY56S7QK8)
Check your Voicemails (#h_01JB0A4ZZEGENKD089CFP7BF07)
Set up your Voicemail Greeting
Navigate to your Personal Settings page and select
Communication > Call & Text > Voice Messages
.
By default, an automated voice greeting message with a male voice will be enabled. If you would prefer the female voice, toggle the male default off and toggle the female default on.
Alternatively, you can record your own personalized voicemail greeting message. To do so, click
Add
to get started. You will be prompted to provide your cell phone number or any number where you are able to receive a phone call. When you answer the call, instructions will tell you exactly what to do. The recording will save to your Inbound Call Voice Message Options.
Check your Voicemails
There are several places to check your voicemails.
(1) Navigate to the Dialer Pad and sort by Voice Messages. Note: The dialer pad is only available with some call packages.
(2) The voicemail can be accessed directly from a lead detail page's Activity Timeline.
(3) Voice messages are available in the Workspace.
Questions?

#### Article 181: Live Call Transferring

- Article ID: `4402253534619`
- Category: `CRM`
- Section: `Calling`
- Updated: `2025-11-10T00:41:43Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/4402253534619-Live-Call-Transferring

Introduction
The live transfer feature is built into the Lofty dialer as a way for calls with leads to be transferred to another team member with your Lofty account. This feature is
not
available on all call packages or all scenarios so please review this document for more information.
Summary
Requirements (#h_01F86BGYKJG8RX526G7RS0D8GM)
How It Works (#h_01F86BH29Q6XB6G187W58XAX5Q)
Requirements
Please be aware of the following. . .
Only available on the following call packages:
Elite
Works on both inbound and outbound calls
Works on click-to-call functionality (when clicking from a lead profile to call
one
specific lead) and on call lists.
Only able to transfer calls to other agents within your Lofty team, not outside of your Lofty team
The agent receiving the call does
not
need a call package, but they do need to have their
Bridge Number
set up (
CRM
>
Settings
>
Manage Dialer
>
Bridge Number
).
How It Works
If you are on a call with a lead (that meets all of the requirements above) and you would like to transfer the call to another agent within your team, simply click on the
Transfer
icon in the bottom-right of the dialer panel:
You will then choose who you would like to transfer the call to (that is within your Lofty team):
The above action will automatically dial out to the third person (your colleague within your Lofty team), and the call panel will show who you are dialing out to (agent) and who you are already connected to (lead):
If the other agent does not pick up, the icon will show as red/orange, and you can transfer again if you would like by clicking the
Transfer
icon.
When it connects to the other agent successfully, it will show up with a green icon. There is no separate conversation that happens before the transfer takes place--it simply adds the agent to the conversation.
You then have three options
Stay on the line
. There are now three people on the line and the conversation can continue.
Hang up yourself
. This will allow for you to leave the conversation but the call will continue between the lead and the agent you connected them with.
Hang up
agent
. This option will kick the agent off the call who you had connected to originally as the third participant in the call.
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by a chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

#### Article 182: Receiving Calls from Leads

- Article ID: `115004556986`
- Category: `CRM`
- Section: `Calling`
- Updated: `2025-11-10T00:45:38Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004556986-Receiving-Calls-from-Leads

Introduction
If you have a Call Package, you will want to be prepared for when a lead actually makes a call to your Lofty virtual number so that you can answer the call and document things appropriately in the CRM. This article will be broken down into two sections--what it looks like when a "known lead" (someone you already have in your database) or an "unknown lead" (someone not yet in your database) makes a call to your virtual number.
*IMPORTANT:
Users need to purchase the call package add-on feature in order to use this feature. For more information, please reference
Adding / Removing Call or Text Packages (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360054858692)
.
Summary
Appearance on Phone (#h_01H9H14MD6H16G4ABHQR3D0HYD)
Known Leads (#h_01H9H1SQV8XQS0SZR98VT4J0R7)
Unknown Leads (+ add to existing lead) (#h_01H9H2QXMR72TSSBFV73Q3C3ZD)
Unknown Leads (+ create a new lead) (#h_01H9H14MD7WBHDF7JD43R88DKQ)
Missed Calls (#h_01H9H14MD7P5W179E6PBY9XX1P)
Questions? (#h_01H9H14MD8SEA58K90N54G59Z0)
Appearance on Phone
The incoming call will be received on whichever number is added as the "Bridge Number" under
Settings
>
Communication
>
Call&Text
>
Info & Settings
.
In most scenarios, the "Bridge Number" is your cell phone.
When you get a call from a lead it will show up on your phone as being from the lead's phone number
and
not
from your "Virtual Number." If you have the Lofty mobile app installed on your phone, you may have access to caller identification. See
How to Set Up Caller Identification (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/115001743643)
for more information.
Known Leads
When a lead calls you, the
Incoming Call
tab will appear on the right side of your CRM page. Click the "minimize" arrow to make the call panel small in the bottom-right instead.
When you receive a call, you will be able to see the lead's name, number, and most recent last contact information pulled from the lead profile.
Answer the call on your bridge phone (see
Call/Text Package Settings (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360000306652)
) first, and then the
Inbound call
panel will appear on the CRM. At the top of the panel, you will see the lead’s name, number, and call status.
In the
Outcome
section you can set the following outcomes:
Talked
- Call connected successfully
Voice Message
- Left a voice message
No Answer
- Lead did not answer the call
Bad Number
– Invalid number
DNC Number
- Do not call the number
DNC Contact
– Do not call the contact
You can send a text to the lead during your call. Click
Select Template
to choose a saved text template. You can also add notes in the
Note
section and have those saved to the lead profile after the call is ended and saved successfully.
Above the red
End Call
icon, you will see three buttons:
New Appointment
,
Add a Task
, or
Leave a Voice Message
. For more information on preparing a pre-recorded voice message that can be used, reference
Voice Messages for Inbound & Outbound Calls (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360000315191)
. Pre-recorded messages can only be used for outbound calls, of course.
Once you click the
End Call
icon, the
Call Result
window will appear. Here you can view the call details, call recording (if applicable), call outcomes, notes, texts, appointments, and tasks. You can change the call outcome after the call. You can also send additional text messages, add new tasks, or add appointments after the call.
Before you save the call result please rate the quality of the call. This allows us to provide feedback to our provider and make sure the quality is maintained as high as possible.
After you click
Save
, you can view the call result from the lead’s timeline at any time in the future.
Unknown Leads (+ add to existing lead)
When an unknown lead calls you the
Incoming Call
tab will appear on the right side of your CRM page and the number will be displayed:
Once you answer your phone you can choose to add the number to an existing lead or create a new lead to associate with that number:
If you click
Add to Existing Lead
you can search for a lead and will be able to find the number in the lead’s detail page later as needed.
Once you have saved the number the
Incoming Call
panel will appear.
Unknown Leads (+ create a new lead)
Once you answer the phone, click "
+
Create New Lead"
. The number will automatically be saved and appear on the
People
page. You can then go back and add the lead’s information after the call.
Missed Calls
Missed call notifications are important to pay attention to so you will want to know what they look like. Here is how they will display on the different Lofty interfaces.
Web App
From Known Leads
A missed call notification will be visible at the top right corner of the page. It can also be seen in the notifications as a "Missed Call."
A small red dot will also appear on the "Phone" icon at the bottom-right corner of the page. Click on this icon to go directly to the Call History page (if applicable). The Call History feature is available at the Accelerator call package and above (see
Add Call or Text Packages (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360001515311)
).
From Unknown Leads
In addition to the missed call notification, users can also receive a reminder of "Unknown Inbound #." By clicking this notification, users can create a new lead directly.
The missed call can also be found on the Call History page (if applicable). There is a '+' button on the right of the missed call notification. Clicking on this will allow for a new lead to be created. Note that the Call History feature is available at the Accelerator call package and above (see
Add Call or Text Packages (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360054858692)
).
Mobile App
The same notifications are available for calls from both known and unknown leads. Here is how this displays:
Support Adding Unknown Numbers as New Leads
Many users provided feedback indicating that it was difficult to add a new lead on the mobile app when an unknown number calls or sends a text to the virtual number. Our features have been optimized so that when an unknown number calls the agent, there will be a push notification on the app. With just one top on the phone, the agent can add the number as a new lead.
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by a chat with us through your Lofty CRM.
Related terms: Unknown inbound, unknown lead

#### Article 183: Short Call Duration

- Article ID: `30549114661659`
- Category: `CRM`
- Section: `Calling`
- Updated: `2025-11-10T00:38:59Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/30549114661659-Short-Call-Duration

Introduction
Telecom carriers closely monitor the length of phone calls, often tagging phone numbers associated with short calls as low trust. This can result in being flagged as potential spam and prevent you from reaching your intended recipients. While Lofty will not prevent you from making calls, this article will outline how Lofty informs you of your short call duration percentage and why that is important.
What is a Short Call?
Per Lofty's service provider Twilio, a short call is any phone call that lasts less than six (6) seconds. Lofty offers two (2) calling methods, Bridge and Voice over IP (VoIP). Learn more about Lofty's call functionality here:
“Click to Call” Function (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004541323)
How can I decrease my short call duration percentage?
The best way to decrease your short call percentage is to have prepared
Call Scripts (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360000306052)
when making outbound calls to leads and by manually leaving a voice message, rather than automatically dropping a voice message to a lead's voicemail box, such as the
Slybroadcast Integration (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360034983832)
.
When an inbound phone call is routed to your bridge number, this will count towards your short call duration percentage, so the best practice is to answer that call, whenever possible.
Here are a few other best practices:
Use Strong, Personalized Openers
Hook them fast so they don't hang up. Rather than asking, "Hi, is this John?" start the call with "Hey John, it's Mary from ABC Realty. I just saw you were looking at 123 Main St online. Do you have a minute?"
This makes the call feel relevant, not robotic.
Don't Sound Like a Robot
Avoid sounding like a robot by using a natural pace, smiling when you talk (it works!), and keeping your energy upbeat and warm.
Avoid Leaving Dead Air
Even a half a second of lag can lead sometime to believe they are being auto-dialed, and they hang up. Be prepared to speak the moment the call connects.
Leave Manual Voicemails
Voicemail drops can lead to ultra-short calls. Deliver manual voicemails and keep them personal and useful. Remember, the goal is to get them to call you back!
Focus on Answered Calls
If your call list has not been vetted, you may have a lot of bad phone numbers. Keep a clean call list by only calling verified numbers and prioritize leads who have opted in to be contacted.
Text Before You Call
A quick text will let the recipient know who is calling and why, making it more likely they will answer and stay on the line.
I got an email about my short call duration, what do I need to do?
If you received an email notification from Lofty about your short call duration percentage, we recommend taking action to increase the length of your phone calls. This email will also have a spreadsheet of your short call data, so you can take a look to see if there are any patterns that are contributing to your short call duration percentage.
Lofty will not turn off or diminish your calling ability, the email is just sent as a notice that your short call duration is higher than recommended and action should be taken to protect the integrity of your phone number.
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by a chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

#### Article 185: Voice Messages for Inbound & Outbound Calls

- Article ID: `360000315191`

Introduction
It can be frustrating to call leads when they go straight to voicemail. Recording a new message every time is not only tedious but also time-consuming. Lofty can help you save time by allowing you to pre-record voice messages for more effective use of your time.
To access these options, navigate to
Settings
>
Communication
>
Call & Text
>
Voice Messages
.
Record an Outbound Call Voice Message
*This feature is included in all Lofty call packages.
To add a new Outbound Call Voice Message, click on the "Add" button:
You can record five messages within the Outbound Call Voice Message category.
To record the message, you will need to enter your phone number. You will then receive a call with step-by-step instructions to record the message.
Give the voice message a name and then click on the blue "Save" button. The name can always be adjusted later.
Use the Outbound Call Voice Messages
For outbound calls, you can leave a recorded voicemail instead of recording a new one every time.  After dropping your voice message, the call will disconnect automatically.
Make sure to drop your voice message only after the answering system triggers the "beep."
After selecting the Voice Message option, the names of the recordings you have made will appear for you to choose from.
Record an Inbound Call Voice Message
*This feature is included in all Lofty call packages.
A default always needs to be selected by clicking the toggle to the on position. You can record up to five voice messages to be available for inbound calls.
To record a new message, click on the "Add" button:
To record the message, you will need to enter your phone number, and then you will receive a call with step-by-step instructions to record the message.
Give the voice message a name and then click on the blue "Save" button. The name can always be adjusted later.
Use the Inbound Call Voice Messages
*This feature is included in all Lofty call packages.
When you are unavailable to answer inbound calls, your leads will be directed to your pre-recorded voice message.
Inbound callers will only be directed to Lofty's inbound call voice message if you are not available (if you are not within working/available hours of what you configured on their Lofty account.) If you are available for calls in Lofty, the inbound call will still be bridged to your bridge number reason why your caller will hear the voicemail of your mobile phone (bridge number).
See this article for more information about setting your availability:
Availability (Working Hours) for Phone Calls (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360001571612)
.
Questions?

The "Click-To-Call" function within Lofty will allow users to call leads directly from their lead profiles easily. For this feature to work, the user must have a Call Package associated with their account. For more information on getting a Call Package added, please see this article:

.

The most accessible option is to navigate to the
People
page and then click on the "phone" icon in the "Communications" column. This will allow you to trigger a phone call directly to that lead.

Call Process
Calling in Bridge Mode
When calling in Bridge Mode, the system will first call the number you saved in
Settings > Communication > Call & Text > Info & Settings > Outbound Call Type
and then connect you to the lead's number you are calling. In other words, the system will call you first at the Bridge Number, and then it will call the lead's number.
Once the call has started, a
call panel will appear on the right side. You can click the minimize option in the top-right to minimize the panel if needed. Here you will see the lead’s name, number, and call status. Below, you will see notes on all of the sections visible in the call panel.
(A) Outcome:
Talked - Call connected successfully and you spoke to the lead
Voice Message - Left a voice message
No Answer - The lead did not answer the call
Bad Number – Invalid number

ot

all number

o

ot

all contacts

. You can add a note for this phone call with any important information you want to save for later. You can edit/add this note later if necessary.
(C)
Send a Text
. You can send a text during the call by typing in the message or clicking
Select Template
to choose a saved text template.
(D)
New Appointment
. This will add a task to your Google Calendar (if integrated) and will also send out an external invite to the lead at their email address.

fter you click

you can view the

on the lead’s timeline. You can listen to the recorded call if the feature is turned on as well as make any additional notes if so desired.
Calling in VOIP Mode
The calling mode can be switched freely between Bridge and VOIP before each call is made. VOIP can be set by navigating to
Settings > Communication > Call & Text > Info & Settings > Outbound Call Type
Calling over VOIP Mode is the same as calling over Bridge Mode; however, the call will connect directly via your browser, rather than connecting to your bridge number first. VOIP is currently only available for outbound calls. All inbound calls will still ring to the number provided under
Incoming Call Type
.
VOIP Mode calls are made through the browser, so an internet connection is required. If the internet connection is weak, we recommend switching to Bridge Mode before making a call. While you can navigate around the CRM without disrupting the call, if the browser is refreshed or closed during a VOIP call, the call will be disconnected.
The Audio Settings are available to set the microphone and speakers when calling over VOIP mode. The microphone and speakers can be changed mid-call, without disruption.

#### Article 187: 10DLC Best Practices

- Article ID: `48036961381659`
- Category: `CRM`
- Section: `Compliance`
- Updated: `2026-03-19T23:35:51Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/48036961381659-10DLC-Best-Practices

Introduction
This guide walks through the steps required to successfully register a 10DLC brand and campaign through Lofty, in the order you will actually complete them. Start by preparing your website before registering anything — reviewers will verify your website as part of the approval process, so it needs to be ready first.
Phase 1: Prepare Your Website (#Phase-1:-Prepare-Your-Website)
Phase 2: Determine Your Brand Type and Register Your Brand (#Phase-2:-Determine-Your-Brand-Type-and-Register-Your-Brand)
Phase 3: Configure Your Campaign (#Phase-3:-Configure-Your-Campaign)
Phase 1: Prepare Your Website
Before starting any registration, make sure your website meets Twilio’s requirements. This is the foundation that reviewers will check against everything else you submit.
Step 1 — Website and Consent Requirements
Before setting up your checkboxes, verify the following on your website first. These items will be cross-checked against your brand and campaign registration during review.
Requirement
Details
Website URL
Confirm your site loads correctly at the exact URL you plan to register. Check whether it works with or without
www
— these are treated as different URLs by
TCR
. Make sure there are no redirects to another domain and that the
SSL
certificate is valid for the registered URL.
Input Phone Field
The input phone field on your website registration form should not be required to fill.
Brand Name visible on website
(Standard Brand)
Your legal business name must be visibly present in the page title, header, footer, or logo. This must match the name you register in Step 3. Legal suffixes such as
LLC
or Inc may be omitted when comparing, but the core name must be identical.
Agent Name visible on website
(Sole Proprietor)
The agent’s legal personal name (First + Last) must appear visibly on the website — for example in the page title, agent bio, or footer. If
TCR
cannot find this name on the page, identity verification will fail. Do not use a team name or brokerage name in place of the agent’s legal name.
Consent checkboxes:
All SMS consent checkboxes must be unchecked by default and must not be required to submit the form. The phone number field must also be optional. A user must be able to enter their phone number and submit the form without checking the SMS consent checkbox — checking it is always the user’s choice. Use the exact wording below for your campaign use case.
Sole Proprietor Use Case
Marketing Use Case (Standard Brand)
Checkbox #1 (optional)
“By checking this box, I agree to receive text messages from [agentName] regarding real estate services, property inquiries, scheduling, and related communications. Message frequency varies. Message and data rates may apply. Reply HELP for help or STOP to opt out.”
“By checking this box, I agree to receive recurring marketing communication from [CompanyName], including auto-dialed calls, texts, and artificial/prerecorded voice messages (message frequency varies; data rates may apply; reply “STOP” to opt-out of texts or “HELP” for assistance); Consent not required to make a purchase. I understand that I can call XXX-XXX-XXXX to obtain direct assistance.”
Checkbox #2
“By checking this box, I agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy of this website.”
“By checking this box, I agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy of this website.”
The exact wording of your checkboxes will be quoted verbatim in your campaign’s opt-in description (Step 4). Finalize the wording before moving on.
Policies:
Your website must include both a Privacy Policy and Terms of Service, with working links to both. See Step 2 for the specific SMS-related content each policy must contain.
Step 2 — Privacy Policy and Terms of Service: SMS Requirements
Your Privacy Policy and Terms of Service must each contain specific SMS-related language. Add a dedicated
“SMS / Text Messaging”
section to your Privacy Policy with the following content:
Privacy Policy — required SMS section:
A statement that users can opt out by replying STOP to any text message. This must be specific to SMS — a general “opt out of advertising” clause does not count.
The following data-sharing clause:
“Text messaging originator opt-in data and consent will not be shared with any third parties.”
Terms of Service — required SMS additions:
“Carriers are not liable for delayed or undelivered messages.”
Instructions for STOP (to opt out) and HELP (for assistance).
“Message and data rates may apply.”
Phase 2: Determine Your Brand Type and Register Your Brand
Your brand type determines everything downstream — including which campaign type you will register and what kind of messages you can send. The key question is whether your business has an EIN (Employer Identification Number).
Step 3 — Choose Your Brand Type and Complete Registration
Use the decision below to identify which path applies to you, then fill in your registration information accordingly.
Standard Brand
Sole Proprietor Brand
EIN required?
Yes
No
Campaign type
Standard Campaign (Marketing)
Sole Proprietor Campaign
Message style
Marketing-focused: listings, open houses, and market updates
Personal and one-to-one: direct outreach about a specific inquiry or property
Once you know your brand type, complete your registration using the following information requirements. All information must be real, consistent, and verifiable — reviewers cross-check submissions against public records.
Field
Standard Brand
Sole Proprietor Brand
Name / EIN
Use the exact legal business name tied to your EIN — not a team name,
DBA
, or marketing name, unless that is also the registered legal entity name.
Use the agent’s
legal personal name
(first + last). Do not use a team name or brokerage name, and do not append business suffixes such as
LLC
or Inc. — the name entered must be the agent’s legal personal name only. This personal name must also be searchable and visible on the website (e.g. in the page title, agent bio, or footer)
Address
Provide a real physical address. An office address is preferred, but a home address is acceptable. Do not use a
PO
Box.
Same as Standard Brand.
Phone Number
Use the agent’s real personal mobile number. Do not use a Twilio number, Google Voice, or any
VoIP
or virtual number.
Same as Standard Brand.
Email
Use a real, monitored business email. A domain-matched email (e.g. name@yourbrand.com) is best. Gmail, Outlook, or Yahoo addresses can work, but the email address must be publicly visible on the website — for example, on the contact or about page.
Same as Standard Brand.
Phase 3: Configure Your Campaign
Once your brand is registered, you will configure your campaign. The following steps cover what Twilio reviewers specifically check during campaign approval.
Step 4 — Opt-in Description
Your “How do consumers opt in?” description must accurately reflect your actual website flow and be verifiable by reviewers. Clearly state where the opt-in happens, describe the consent action (the checkbox), and paste the checkbox text
exactly as it appears on your website
— do not paraphrase. If you send recurring messages, note that frequency varies.
If the opt-in occurs behind a login or offline, provide a public URL with screenshots of the relevant pages.
The opt-in description should follow one of these two formats depending on your form type:
One-step form
(all fields including phone appear on a single form):
“Consumers opt in by completing the contact form at {WEBSITE_URL}. The form displays a checkbox stating: ‘[EXACT MARKETING CHECKBOX TEXT FROM WEBSITE]’. Checking this box is optional. Phone number is optional.”
Two-step form
(email entered first, then full form with phone and checkboxes on step 2):
“Consumers opt in by completing the two-step contact form at {WEBSITE_URL}. On the first step, they enter their email address and click Continue. The second step displays their full contact details along with a checkbox stating: ‘[EXACT MARKETING CHECKBOX TEXT FROM WEBSITE]’. Checking this box is optional. Phone number is optional.”
All checkboxes are unchecked by default and are not required. The phone number field is optional. Message frequency varies. Message & data rates may apply. Reply STOP to opt out and HELP for help.
Step 5 — Writing Sample Messages
Twilio requires 2–5 sample messages. Each sample should reflect what you actually send, identify the sender by brand name, and use square brackets for variable content such as [First Name] or [City]. At least one sample should contain an opt-out instruction such as “Reply STOP to opt out.”
Important:
A system opt-out message is automatically appended to every message by the platform. Do not include it inside your sample messages.
Use the description and sample templates below for your campaign type:
Standard Campaign (Marketing)
Sole Proprietor Campaign
Description template
“[COMPANY_NAME] uses this campaign to send real estate marketing messages to leads who have opted in via the contact form on our website. Messages include new property listings, price drop alerts, market updates, and open house invitations for buyers and sellers in [AREA].”
“[AGENT NAME] uses this campaign for personalized 1-on-1 SMS with individual clients who have opted in via the contact form on their website. Messages are direct outreach regarding specific properties and real estate needs — not bulk or automated broadcasts.”
Sample messages
“Hi [First Name], new listing alert in [City]! A [X]-bed home just hit the market at $[Price]. Want to schedule a showing? — [Agent] with [COMPANY_NAME]. Reply with “unsubscribe” to opt-out of future text communication. This message is sent from [COMPANY_NAME].”
“Hi [First Name], a home matching your search just dropped $[X]K in price this week. Interested in taking a look? — [Agent] with [COMPANY_NAME]. Reply with “unsubscribe” to opt-out of future text communication. This message is sent from [COMPANY_NAME].”
“Hi [First Name], this is [Agent Name]. I saw you were looking at properties in the area — do you have a few minutes to chat about what you’re searching for? Reply with “unsubscribe” to opt-out of future text communication. This message is sent from [Agent Name].”
“Hi [First Name], just following up on the property you inquired about. Are you still interested? Happy to answer any questions. — [Agent Name]. Reply with “unsubscribe” to opt-out of future text communication. This message is sent from [Agent Name].”
Step 6 — STOP and HELP Keywords
Users must always be able to text STOP to opt out of messages and HELP to receive assistance. If you send a welcome or confirmation message as part of a recurring program, that message should include your brand name, a note on message frequency, instructions for STOP and HELP, and a data rates disclosure.
Step 7 — Consistency Check Before Submitting
One of the most common reasons campaigns are rejected is inconsistency across the submission. Before submitting, verify that all of the following match each other:
What to check
Must be consistent with
Where verified
Registered brand name
Website page title / header / footer
Step 1
Website URL in registration
Actual serving URL — exact www / non-www
Step 1
Checkbox text on website
Opt-in description in campaign
Step 1
Campaign description
Sample messages — same use case, same brand name
Step 5
Privacy Policy & Terms of Service
SMS compliance requirements
Step 2
If you use a
DBA
or display name that differs from your legal entity name, explain the relationship in your campaign description and make sure the name is visible on the website. Before submitting, prepare your evidence as one package: opt-in screenshots, checkbox text, Privacy Policy and Terms of Service links, and sample messages.
Reference resources from Twilio
The following Twilio documentation pages contain useful diagrams and expanded guidance. Open each page and click “Expand image” to view the relevant screenshots:
Brand type selection flowchart —
Programmable Messaging and A2P 10DLC (https://www.twilio.com/docs/messaging/compliance/a2p-10dlc)
Campaign registration page sections —
Direct Sole Proprietor Registration Overview (https://www.twilio.com/docs/messaging/compliance/a2p-10dlc/direct-sole-proprietor-registration-overview)
Opt-in mechanism requirements and hosted screenshots guidance —
Gather the Required Business Information (https://www.twilio.com/docs/messaging/compliance/a2p-10dlc/collect-business-info)

#### Article 188: A2P 10DLC - What It Is & Which Plan to Choose

- Article ID: `17141883940379`
- Category: `CRM`
- Section: `Compliance`
- Updated: `2026-04-17T21:00:31Z`

Introduction
This article explains what A2P 10DLC is, who needs to register, types of brands and campaign, pricing, trust scores, and includes some frequently asked questions.
Summary
What is A2P 10DLC? (#h_01KMGVTT4HVBYEY5YQRHC1PG7Z)

What is A2P 10DLC?
A2P (Application to Person) 10DLC is the US carrier standard for business text messaging. All texts sent from Lofty are considered A2P — they come from software, not a personal phone. Carriers require registration to verify who is messaging consumers and why, reduce spam, and enable reliable delivery.
You must register if
You send text messages to US phone numbers via Lofty (including AI Assistant texts).
You do not need to register if
You never text US phone numbers.
If You're outside the US/Canada but text US numbers — you must first set up a US LLC. Contact support@lofty.com for help.
Note:
Toll-free numbers are not part of the A2P 10DLC system. Contact Lofty Support separately.
Brands and Campaigns — The Two Parts of Registration

Tip: If you expect to exceed 6,000 messages/day in the future, register Plan B now. Campaign use cases can't be changed after approval, and resubmission costs another fee.
Secondary Vetting & Trust Scores (Standard Plans B & C)
Secondary vetting is a one-time $40/brand carrier review. It produces a Trust Score (0–100) that determines your T-Mobile limits and message speed. Trust Scores don't change automatically — if yours is too low, you must submit a new secondary vetting request.

Managing Your Registration After Approval
Go to Settings → Call/Text Settings → 10DLC Compliance to:
View all brands, their status, type, and creation date
Click a brand to see its campaigns and linked phone numbers
Move phone numbers between campaigns
Share a campaign with other Lofty users via the permissions cog
FAQs
Do I need a separate 10DLC campaign for each Lofty drip campaign?
No. Most users only need one 10DLC campaign. A 10DLC campaign represents your reason for texting, not a specific Smart Plan or drip sequence.
I already registered through another vendor. Do I need to register again in Lofty?
Yes. Brands and campaigns are vendor-specific and cannot be transferred. Registering via Lofty sets Lofty as your vendor automatically.
I'm in Canada — does this apply to me?
Only if your virtual numbers text US phone numbers. Canadian-only texting doesn't require 10DLC registration.
How long does approval take?
Typically 3–5 business days, but can take up to 4–5 weeks.
When am I charged the monthly fee?
On the 1st of each month. The fee is waived during your registration month — you first pay it the month after your campaign is verified. If the campaign fails, no monthly fee is charged.
Can I get a refund if my registration fails?
No. Payment goes directly to The Campaign Registry, not to Lofty. Fees are non-refundable.
Which address should I use?
Use the address on your EIN/Tax ID letter.
Questions?

#### Article 189: DNC.com (Contact Center Compliance) Integration

- Article ID: `35209288678555`
- Category: `CRM`
- Section: `Compliance`
- Updated: `2025-11-10T01:04:15Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/35209288678555-DNC-com-Contact-Center-Compliance-Integration

Introduction
Lofty has a direct integration with DNC.com (also known as Contact Center Compliance) that you can utilize to to connect the National DNC, state DNCs, and known litigator lists into the Lofty platform. In order to do so, you must meet both of these requirements:
You must have a SAN generated by the National Do Not Call Registry. You can learn more about this here:
https://telemarketing.donotcall.gov/
. You will need this
before
subscribing to DNC.com.
You must have a separate subscription with DNC.com.
Schedule an appointment with them (https://meetings.hubspot.com/ashley-huggins?uuid=816ad879-1658-4ed4-b21a-d03ca884168e)
or
review their website (https://www.dnc.com/)
to learn more. DNC.com will provide you with a certain number of "scrubs" and these will be utilized in Lofty to scrub phone numbers (see details below for how it works).
*IMPORTANT
:
All the information shared in this article represents product functionality information only. This is not legal advice. You must obtain your own legal advice regarding all federal and local laws/regulations for call and text compliance.
Summary
DNC.com Integration Settings (#h_01JPXB90VGBP0FMKEFEF5C2B5S)
How the Integration Works (#h_01JPXD338GH86W2DAF1F7GR7BE)
Internal DNC List Sync (#h_01K36PY8FZ96BN0KTS6GF4V7W6)
Best Practices During a Government Shutdown (#h_01K6NC3DQ7E30B6XRXM8CGEB5Q)
DNC.com Integration Settings
To integrate your DNC.com account with Lofty, click 'Connect' on the integrations or marketplace page:
Here, you will need to provide your DNC.com account name, API key, and the Project ID. Note, the Project ID is only required if you want to link a specific project. If this field is left empty, your master project will be configured.
Once you have finished integrating your DNC.com account with Lofty, you will be asked to choose how you would like DNC.com results codes to behave in Lofty. The DNC.com integration with Lofty will return a status code when a number is checked. Please contact
support@dnc.com (mailto:support@dnc.com)
regarding any questions for these status codes.
When the 'Safe' toggle is turned ON for a specific status, Lofty will NOT warn you prior to calling or texting these numbers because it has been marked as "safe."
You can edit these preferences at any time by selecting "Configure DNC.com settings"
How the Integration Works
Once integrated, a "DNC.com Status" will be listed with every phone number (see screenshot below). This will provide the status returned by DNC.com, but only if the number has been checked. It will also list the last time that status is updated.
For any call or text you are making to a phone number in your system with the status of "Unknown Consent," the DNC.com integration will process a "scrub" to determine if there are any results from DNC.com that you want to be aware of.  All other statuses representing consent received (System Recorded Consent, User Recorded Consent, Business Relationship) will
not
trigger the DNC.com scrub.
If the phone number has been scrubbed already within the last 30 days, it will
not
be scrubbed again if you are trying to make a phone call or send a text. The system will check the "Last Updated" field to check this. Most DNC lists must be checked every 30 days for any changes which is why this logic exists.
If the status returned from DNC.com is considered 'unsafe,' Lofty will present you with a warning. One example can be seen in the following screenshot. You can still choose to proceed with the call/text but should pay attention to the warning and how it applies to your situation before doing so.
If a phone number has been determined by the integration to be 'unsafe,' all Smart Plan (or other) auto texts in the Lofty platform will be converted into manual text tasks for manual review to avoid automated texts being sent to someone on a DNC list.
Internal DNC List Sync
Lofty will automatically sync your
Internal DNC (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/35314857154075)
list to your DNC.com project. Important note - only numbers with a +1 country code will be synced.
Best Practices During a Government Shutdown
During a government shutdown, the FTC may not be actively maintaining the federal Do Not Call Registry. Outlined below are some best practice compliance steps you can take to protect yourself.
1. Continue scrubbing against the most recent national DNC data available
Use your last updated FTC registry file from before the outage.
Maintain integration with DNC.com so you still remove known DNC numbers.
2. Scrub against state-specific DNC lists as usual
State registries remain operational unless separately affected.
Many state lists include additional DNC numbers not in the federal list.
3. Honor your internal DNC list
Always suppress numbers where the lead has directly opted out with you, regardless of national or state database access.
4. Apply extra caution with cold prospecting
If your risk tolerance is low, consider limiting calls to only those who have consented to be contacted by you.
5. Document compliance actions during the outage
Keep records showing you scrubbed with the most recent available data from the FTC.
Note dates of your last download and any operational limitations caused by the shutdown.
Maintain calling logs and suppression reports.
6. Monitor for FTC service restoration
As soon as the FTC DNC Registry comes back online, update your data immediately.
Refresh integrations with the new copy to catch any numbers registered during the outage period.
7. Train calling staff on modified compliance rules during the shutdown
Explain that new leads may have registered but are not yet in your suppression lists.
Reinforce opt-out handling and prompt honoring of any DNC requests received live.
Bottom line:
You
can
keep running your scrubs via DNC.com integrations using the last available dataset, but you should treat the outage as a heightened-risk period and tighten calling criteria until the national list is refreshed.
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

#### Article 190: Do Not Contact Settings

- Article ID: `35314857154075`
- Category: `CRM`
- Section: `Compliance`
- Updated: `2025-11-10T00:52:46Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/35314857154075-Do-Not-Contact-Settings

Introduction
*IMPORTANT
: This article is for informational purposes only and does not substitute consultation with appropriate legal counsel regarding this topic. It is your responsibility to comply with federal, state, local, or other laws and regulations related to all outgoing communication.
The Do Not Contact setting page allows you to organize your Internal Do Not Contact list, as well as upload any National or State DNC lists that you subscribe to. This article outlines how Lofty treats the phone numbers that are on these lists.
Summary
Adding Numbers to a Do Not Contact List (#h_01JQ74GRD72M9ERGXEESSG99BT)
Do Not Contact Lists (#h_01JQ9TBR46PQBABJBTC2HZCD07)
Calling or Texting a Number on a DNC List (#h_01JQ9TK5AMNV3KH710M6K4C3J0)
DNC Scrub Integrations (#h_01JQ9TRDKQ8Z6PS24P9M1JRDS3)
Adding Numbers to a Do Not Contact List
Lofty offers the ability to add both Internal Do Not Contact numbers as well as National and State DNC lists. To access the Do Not Contact list navigate to
Settings → Call & Text → Do Not Contact Settings
.
Click
+ Add New
to manually add a number to the Internal DNC list. When you manually add a number, it can only be added to the Internal DNC list.
Click
Import a List
to upload a file with numbers to the Internal DNC list, the National DNC list, or to the State DNC list.
Note: When uploading a list, the maximum file size is 1GB. Please contact
support@lofty.com (mailto:support@lofty.com)
to upload a larger list.
Only the account admin is able to add or remove numbers from the DNC lists.
When uploading a DNC list, a pop-up will ask what type of DNC list you are importing and how you want these numbers to display in your account. You have the option to override existing consent statuses for the phone numbers that belong to leads in your system.
Selecting 'Yes' on any of these existing consent statuses will change the current phone number consent status to
Do Not Call
. If a lead is added and their phone number is on a DNC list, their phone consent status will automatically be Do Not Call.
Do Not Contact Lists
Lofty offers four (4) different options for Do Not Contact Lists: Internal, National, State, and Other.
Internal Do Not Contact List
The internal DNC list includes phone numbers who have opted out of being contacted by you or your business specifically. These numbers may or may not be included on a national or state DNC registry.
National, State, or Other DNC Lists
Phone numbers that are on a National, State, or Other DNC list have registered their phone number with a DNC registry. It's important to scrub numbers against these databases, as the owners of these phone numbers have expressed that they do not want to be contacted by businesses that they have not given consent to be contacted by.
Calling or Texting a Number on a DNC List
Phone numbers that are on a DNC list
cannot
be called or texted. These numbers will have their call & text communication consent set to Do Not Call and can be filtered on the people page using the TCPA Number Consent filter.
While only the account admin can fully remove a phone number from the DNC lists, if you have consent to contact a lead who's phone number is on a DNC list, you can change the phone number consent status to something other than Do Not Call to call or text that lead. This action will not affect any other leads that may have the same phone number on their profile.
DNC Scrub Integrations
Lofty integrates directly with DNC.com. Learn more here:
DNC.com (Contact Center Compliance) Integration (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/35209288678555)
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your Lofty CRM.
