#### Article 372: Agent Websites

- Article ID: `360054744232`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `Agent Subdomain`
- Updated: `2025-11-11T02:55:20Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360054744232-Agent-Websites

Introduction
Agent Websites are designed to be quick and easy to build, but still provide a location for agents to use for marketing their business as part of an office or company (parent site) using Lofty. An Agent Website has limitations on what can be edited, but does not have to go through a complex or extended MLS application process (as long as the MLS does not require individual applications for subdomain websites). There is no additional cost associated for these sites.
Summary
What can be edited on an Agent Website? (#h_01JZTYJJ2GJC7HW5ZRVHZH6DNY)
Domain Configuration for Website Creation (#h_01EW453CQHNR5D3AHB2C0HT5ER)
Manage Agent Website Creation Settings (#id-3/4/2021:FeatureReleaseTrainingforCRM3.21,Site5.9-TeamOwner)
Auto-Creation vs. Manual Creation (#h_01JZTXG409VTHEKEPQDPMVYSAX)
Website Sync Mode (#h_01JZTXH8D47TT0WTJGFB1N7JMN)
Common Troubleshooting (#id-3/4/2021:FeatureReleaseTrainingforCRM3.21,Site5.9-TeamMember/Agent)
FAQs (#h_01EWBA6AGD7B48R7H0AYDYAXCZ)
What can be edited on an Agent Website?
When an Agent Website is auto-created, it will copy the appearance of the Company, Office, or Team website above it.
If unlocked at the parent website level (see
Website Sync Mode (#h_01JZTXH8D47TT0WTJGFB1N7JMN)
) the following blocks and sections can be edited by the agent:
Feature
Permission/Behavior
Header
Optional (Can choose to edit or keep synced)
Footer
Always synced from the parent website
Menu
✅
Rename
✅
Move
✅
Hide
❌
Delete
❌
Add New Pages
❌
Add New Folders
Block Library
✅Can add the below blocks with limited styles:
Hero
Agent
Review
Featured Area
Home Valuation
Featured Listings
Blog
Form
Style
❌
SEO Settings & Advanced SEO Tool
❌
Blog
✅
Featured Area
✅ (Maximum of 6 allowed)
Registration Popup
❌ Style synced from parent site on creation
Lead Registration Rules
❌
Subdomain Prefix
If you would like to change the prefix of your website, which is typically in the format of
firstlast.url.com
, you can do so by navigating to
Settings > Basic Info > Subdomain
Personal Information
This information is what displays on any blocks that show agent information, including the chat box, listing detail page, About page, etc. Edit this under
Settings > Company Info > Agents > Edit
Lead Source
The default setting for the lead source will always be the same as the parent website. If you would like to change this, you can customize it under
Settings
>
Lead Capture
>
Lead Source
:
Integrations
The following integrations can be set up individually for your website:
Google Analytics Integration (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360038373351)
Google Tag Manager (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360042831291)
Google Ads (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/26883984829083)
Facebook Pixel Integration (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360038005452)
Adwerx Integration (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/20611002129819)
Follow-Up Boss Integration (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/24974165532443)
Listings Block & Listing Filters
To have your listings prioritized when displayed in the listings blocks, make sure your license ID and MLS ID are present under
CMS > Listing > MLS Integration
, as outlined
HERE (#h_01F1DY5RW6QTB46082DMVQBSH1)
.
You do have access to edit the
All Listings
and
Sold Listings
filters. You can edit these filters by going to
Listings
>
Filters
:
Domain Configuration for Website Creation
The following requirements have to be met for an Agent Website to be created automatically:
The Lofty Parent Website (associated with the Parent Site Owner/Admin seat)
must
have its vanity domain. For example, www.abcrealestate.com. Note that third-level domains (search.abcrealestate.com) are not allowed to have websites underneath them.
The domain configuration on the Parent Website vanity domain must allow Lofty to build subdomains. Refer to the
Domain Configuration Guide (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360054554712)
for more information.
Your MLS must allow Lofty to build subdomains without requiring any additional applications.
Please note that using "firstlast.domain.com" will only be an option once the parent site domain is configured as a vanity domain (e.g. lofty.
realestate.com)
AND
a wildcard CNAME has been added to the domain settings as seen below:
Name = *
Value = yourdomain.com
As long as the above conditions are met, users who are added by the Account Owner will also have an agent website created for them. This user will also receive an email letting them know their subdomain has been created.
Manage Agent Website Creation Settings
Auto-Creation vs. Manual Creation
Agent Websites will auto-create when the agent activates their Lofty account for the first time.
If you would like to manually control when the Agent Websites are created, you can modify the auto-creation policy in the CMS Site List.
Click on
Website
>
Create Agent Website(s)
, then the settings wheel next to
Create Agent Websites
.
The system will then check the criteria to make sure the agent website can be created. If it
cannot
be created, specific feedback will be given as to why. Some scenarios include the Parent Website not being on a vanity domain, CNAME settings not being configured correctly, etc.
Website Sync Mode
Agent Websites inherit their appearance from the Team, Office, or Company website above them by default. But you can adjust this setting to give your agents greater control over the appearance of their website.
Common Troubleshooting
MLS Configuration
To ensure compliance with your MLS, you will need to add your Agent ID to display MLS data. The MLSs available to you will be the same ones that the owner of the parent website applied for, but your website will only display the data for the MLSs that you are a member of. Navigate to
Listings > MLS > MLS Integration
and add your Agent ID to the MLS that can be displayed on your website.
A pop-up will allow you to search for yourself and confirm your Agent ID. Once you have verified your MLS membership, the MLS data will display on your website!
If you would like to manually add a deleted MLS back, click on the blue
Add a New MLS
button. Please note that you can only do so if that
MLS is already connected to the parent website.
If your MLS requires an application to be submitted to build an Agent Website, Lofty can help with that process manually. Lofty is aware of the MLSs that have this requirement and will not allow for an Agent Website that needs individual MLS review to be
created automatically (#h_01EW453CQHNR5D3AHB2C0HT5ER)
or
manually (#h_01EW453GK2Z1PBHSWAHY0NE1DT)
. Because of the application process, it may take longer to go through the setup process.
Landing Page Creation
If a Lofty user/agent goes to access the landing page tool or clicks on the CMS, but they do not have an Agent Website, they will be presented with a screen showing the option to create a landing page using the Account Owner's site.
Just like when the Account Owner tries to create a website, logic will be in place to explain why it is
not
possible in some scenarios (i.e., third-level domain, CNAME, lofty.com, etc.).
A Company Owner/Admin can remove this access by changing the
Edit Own Website
permission for individual users (see
Organization - Permission Profiles (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/4407530443291)
).
Agent Website Deactivation
Please note that an Agent Website will be deleted automatically in the following scenarios:
The agent who owns the Agent Website is removed from the account.
The parent website (Company, Office, or Team) is deleted, or access to Lofty is revoked.
FAQs
As an agent, what if I would like more control over my website than what is currently available for an Agent Website? (#h_01EWBATWQH7NCSZFZJ9EFJEVR6)
As a Company Owner/Admin, what if I already have agents on my account but no agent websites set up? (#h_01EWBA5T5X8HDBZXHACHGZ7FJ0)
Can individual agents run Lofty lead generation campaigns using an Agent Website? Or does it have to be an Agent Website with a Vanity domain? (#h_01EWBAV8B2KDZ8V8JY3HH9C3PP)
What if my agent does not need an Agent Website? (#h_01EWBAVEEY6BSG6YH5J73G3F16)
What is the difference between a subdomain and a third-level domain? (#h_01EWBAVN2EAX8PX47X6AETCBK9)
How can I customize the navigation and add pages, blocks, etc., to my agent website? (#h_01EWBAVVMMYGT1M2DMJNRPWYNM)
How do I get an Agent Website if my Team Website is not on a "vanity domain"? (#h_01EWBAW0K7DAB4ABFGZ8NQCJ77)
Where does the Agent Website's contact info in the footer sync from? (#h_01FARQWPR0K83FP53K7VXYS5KT)
As an agent, what if I would like more control over my website?
Consider unlocking Full SEO. Please check with your Account Owner/Admin if you are unable to find the option to upgrade.
As a Company Owner/Admin, what if I already have agents on my account but no Agent Websites set up?
As soon as the requirements are met (outlined at the beginning of the article), websites will be created for existing agents as well as new agents. The main requirement that has to be met is that of the domain configuration. See
Domain Configuration Guide: Agent Website(s) (https://help.chime.me/hc/en-us/articles/360054554712#h_01EVHM2584HMXKD4J9GPJQ2RRN)
.
Can individual agents run Lofty lead generation campaigns using a subdomain?
Yes. Lofty lead generation
can
be run using a subdomain website (described in this article). Agent Websites with Full SEO unlocked will allow for additional customization to the website and landing pages for campaigns that agents might be running individually and not via Lofty. If you are interested in Lofty lead generation, navigate to the Lofty Marketplace to request more information:
What is the difference between a subdomain and a third-level domain?
*IMPORTANT
: Lofty subdomains can only be third-level domains.
A
subdomain
is a domain that is part of a larger domain. For example, west.example.com, go.link.example.com, and east.example.com are subdomains of the example.com domain.
A
third-level domain
is a specific subdomain that has only 3 parts. For example, west.example.com, go.example.com, and east.example.com are third-level domains (and even subdomains) of the example.com domain, but go.link.example.com is a subdomain, but it is
not
a third-level domain as it has four parts (meaning it is a fourth-level domain).
How do I get a website if the parent website is not on a "vanity domain"?
Unfortunately, Lofty will
not
be able to build an Agent website if this is the case. You may want to consider an Agent Website with Vanity Domain (see
Websites on Lofty (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/37950239399451)
), and you can use either the provided "lofty.com" domain or you can use your own if you have one.
Where does the Agent Website's contact info in the footer sync from?
The Agent Website's contact information will sync directly from the parent website. In other words, the parent website has a configuration for selecting the profile that will be displayed in the footer, and any changes made here will also reflect automatically on the Agent website footer.
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

### Section: Agent/Group Website

#### Article 373: Understanding Website Options: Agent Websites vs. Vanity Domain Sites vs. Full SEO Sites

- Article ID: `360055394331`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `Agent/Group Website`
- Updated: `2025-11-20T20:33:37Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360055394331-Understanding-Website-Options-Agent-Websites-vs-Vanity-Domain-Sites-vs-Full-SEO-Sites

Introduction
When building your online presence with Lofty, you have three main website options. Each serves a different purpose and offers varying levels of customization, branding, and SEO capabilities. This article covers what you need to know.
Summary
Agent Websites (#h_01KAHD06TKRP1811ZYNWBS0Z9H)
Vanity Domain Sites (#h_01KAHDP6WC3EG9HT613S8P0Y1C)
Full SEO Sites (#h_01KAHE9373V6HAC6AXJZ8RTYJW)
Quick Comparison Table (#h_01KAHEG90TY6Y8AWGRBC7YSBTX)
Which Option Should You Choose? (#h_01KAHEPMZJNBZPF6YXN0024JK8)
Agent Websites
What it is:
An Agent Website is the most basic option, designed to give agents a quick and easy way to establish an online presence. These sites are typically created automatically when an agent activates their Lofty account.
Agent Websites are a carbon copy of its parent website.
Key Features:
Domain:
Uses a subdomain, like firstname.companyname.com.
Cost:
Included at no extra charge.
Customization:
Limited. You can edit basic elements like the header and hero section but cannot add custom pages.
MLS Integration:
Inherits MLS feeds from the parent site (Full SEO Website).
SEO:
Minimal. No individual SEO optimization tools.
Best For:
Agents who need a simple, functional site without investing in branding or advanced marketing features.
Vanity Domain Sites
What it is:
A Vanity Domain upgrade allows you to replace your subdomain with a custom domain, like yourname.com. This is a branding enhancement that makes your site look more professional and easier for clients to remember.
Vanity Domain Sites start as a carbon copy of its parent website, but have a custom domain and can be edited.
Key Features:
Domain:
Custom vanity domain.
Cost:
$20/month.
Customization:
Moderate. You can edit navigation, add custom pages, and personalize templates.
MLS Integration:
Inherits MLS feeds from the parent site (Full SEO Website).
SEO:
Basic SEO tools available, but not as comprehensive as Full SEO sites.
Best For:
Agents who want their website to reflect their branding, without customizing an entire website.
Full SEO Sites
What it is:
A Full SEO site is the premium option for agents serious about online marketing. It includes advanced SEO tools, full customization, and enhanced MLS integration.
Full SEO Sites are completely unique and designed by you.
Key Features:
Domain:
Custom vanity domain required.
Cost:
$79/month.
Customization:
Fully editable. Custom pages, blogs, featured areas, scripts, and styles.
MLS Integration:
Must complete MLS applications.
SEO:
Comprehensive SEO checklist, meta tags, keyword optimization, and blog capabilities.
Best For:
Agents who want to maximize lead generation, improve search rankings, and build a strong digital brand
Quick Comparison Table
Feature
Agent Website
Vanity Domain Site
Full SEO Site
Domain
Subdomain
Custom Vanity Domain
Custom Vanity Domain
Cost
Included
Paid Upgrade
Premium Upgrade
Customization
Limited
Moderate
Full
SEO Tools
Minimal
Basic
Advanced
MLS Integation
Inherited
Inherited
Application Required
Which Option Should You Choose?
Agent Website:
If you need a quick, no-cost solution.
Vanity Domain Site:
If branding and professionalism are priorities.
Full SEO Site:
If you want maximum visibility, lead generation, and customization.
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please contact our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your CRM.

column:

URL Slug
"URL Slug" refers to the last part of a URL that is specific to a web page. The default URL Slug is the post title but you can edit this without having to change the post title. The following are supported: letters, numbers, and hyphenated words (e.g. "first-blog-post"). Other characters cannot be recognized and will be changed into hyphens automatically.

SEO

THIS (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360039873672)
article.
To edit the SEO settings for an individual blog post, click on the
SEO
tab:
Meta Title
:
A meta title (also called a title tag) is an element in the head section of an HTML document that defines the title of each page of a website. It is retrieved by web browsers and also used by search engines such as Google to display a webpage in search results (SERPs). The default meta title is in the following format:
Blog Title - Creator Name - Company Name
This can be edited and you can use the tool to "+ Insert variable."
Meta Keywords
:
Meta keywords describe the content of a web page in a short and concise way and should be important indicators of a page's content to search engines. The default meta keywords are blank when you create a new blog post in Lofty but you can add/edit as well as use the "+ Insert variable" tool if needed.
Meta Description
:
A meta description is an HTML element that describes and summarizes the contents of your page for the benefit of users and search engines. The default meta description is the first sentence in the blog post but can be changed by editing and using the "+ Insert variable" tool.

#### Article 376: How to set up the Closely mobile app

- Article ID: `21760812153243`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `Closely`
- Updated: `2025-11-11T09:33:05Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/21760812153243-How-to-set-up-the-Closely-mobile-app

Introduction
Closely is a consumer app designed to streamline the entire home buying or selling process, serving both buyers and sellers. It helps you better manage and facilitate real estate transactions, deliver personalized service, and enhance the client experience. Closely is offered to Lofty clients with a website at no additional cost.
For an introduction to the consumer facing Closely app, please see
Introduction to Closely Mobile App (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360041042691)
Summary
Setting up the Closely App (#h_01HKAMF6AQJ8W3GKE8WJTC9TD4)
How do leads log in or register for the Closely app? (#h_01HKAN509WE9C84VD62PE20CRH)
How do I know if my leads are using the Closely app? (#h_01HKAQKDA3QJVV1Y0M15Y4VFBM)
How do I guide my leads to the Closely app? (#h_01HKANW72NZFRYV0WY25BC9YMD)
What does the Closely app download page look like? (#h_01HKAPX4YA306363BQX2F5N0YP)
Is there an agent version of the Closely app? (#h_01HKAQ2DTXSQ3HQNE2K856W462)
Setting the Closely App Map Search (#h_01HKAMXKCZVJQ59W7TPX2V438V)
Setting up the Closely App
After integrating your MLS and setting up your Lofty built website, the Closely mobile app will automatically be configured for you.
Navigate to
CMS -> Settings -> Lead Capture
.
Here, you will find the Closely toggle switch, which is turned
on
by default. By enabling the Closely app, your website, welcome email, and email alerts will display the QR Code for your leads to download the Closely app.
Toggling off the Closely app switch will remove the Closely app download QR Code from your website and email notifications, however your users can still access the Closely app independently.
How do leads log in or register for the Closely app?
Closely app accounts and Lofty built websites are interconnected. The lead's activity in the Closely app will tracked in the same way their activity is tracked on your Lofty built website.
If your leads have registered on your website, they can use their website credentials to log in to the Closely app.
If a lead has not registered on your Lofty built website, but they do exist in your CRM, they can download the Closely app through the QR code on your website or email notifications or from the invitation link you sent them, and Lofty will connect the existing lead in your CRM with the account they just created on the Closely app.
If a new lead downloads the Closely app via your QR code, and they do not exist in your CRM, they will be created as a new lead in your CRM with the Source listed as
Closely App
.
How do I know if my leads are using the Closely app?
If your lead registered through the Closely app, their source will be marked as "Closely app", as shown above. Any activity performed by your leads using the Closely app will be tagged as "via Closely" in the lead's activity log.
You can also identify Closely users by using the Advanced Filter in the Leads list.
How do I guide my leads to the Closely app?
If the Closely app toggle in the CMS settings is enabled, your website's footer, mobile site's bottom bar, welcome email, alert emails, and home reports will automatically include your Closely app's download QR code or download link.
You can also invite your leads to download Closely manually by sending the Closely app download link via text message. This text message can be sent in mass:
The Closely app download invitation can also be sent to an individual lead:
Please note, the download links on your website, emails, and invitations will contain your agentId parameter to ensure that your leads are matched with you when they log in or register. If a lead downloads the Closely app from the app store, and not from the code or link you provide, Lofty will not be able to identify that this lead belongs to you and the lead will be matched with whichever agent has most recently had this lead register on their Lofty built website.
What does the Closely app download page look like?
After scanning a Closely app download QR code or clicking on the download invitation link, the following download page will open.
The link will automatically detect whether the Closely App has been installed on the device. If Closely is installed, it will prompt to open the app. If it is not downloaded, the system will guide the user to the App Store or Google Play for installation.
Is there an agent version of the Closely app?
No, the Closely app is a consumer facing app, designed to be used by your leads. To experience the Closely app yourself, register as a lead on your website and log in or download the app via your download link.
If your leads send you messages through the Closely app, you can still receive and chat with them through the CRM or the Lofty mobile app.
Setting the Closely App Map Search
The Closely app will by default use the map center point you have set up for your Lofty built website. Navigate to
CMS -> Editor -> All Listings page -> Listing Search -> Map Center Point
to configure the point the map search centers on for both your website and the Closely app.

### Section: Compliance

#### Article 378: Accessibility / ADA / WCAG Solution

- Article ID: `40529369381019`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `Compliance`
- Updated: `2026-01-22T15:24:57Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/40529369381019-Accessibility-ADA-WCAG-Solution

Lofty’s Commitment to Accessibility
Lofty is committed to ensuring our platform is accessible to all users. We take digital accessibility seriously and continuously update our system to align with WCAG 2.1 Level AA standards, which are widely recognized as the benchmark for digital accessibility.
While digital accessibility is an evolving landscape, our goal is to provide a platform that supports inclusive access for all potential home
Understanding ADA Requirements for Real Estate
Real estate professionals need to understand where they fit in the current regulatory landscape. Based on recent Department of Justice (DOJ) rulings, there are key distinctions between government and private entities:
· Private Businesses (Title III): Most real estate brokerages and agents fall under Title III of the ADA. Currently, there is no specific published rule with a technical standard or deadline for private businesses. However, courts increasingly use WCAG 2.1 Level AA as the benchmark in accessibility litigation, making voluntary compliance a best practice.
Government Entities (Title II): Recent rules establish strict compliance deadlines (April 2026 or 2027) for state and local government entities. While this applies to the public sector, it has raised the standard for accessibility expectations across the web.
Platform Accessibility Features
Lofty builds accessibility directly into the foundation of your website rather than relying on superficial fixes.
Default Website Template Features:
The following technical features are automatically implemented and currently live in Lofty's default website template. This ensures that your site starts with a strong baseline for accessibility without requiring manual coding on your part.
· Semantic Markup:
Added semantic markup to designate page elements, including text whose appearance conveys meaning.
· ARIA Implementation:
Using ARIA landmarks and labels to identify regions of a page.
· Data Tables:
Using tables with captions and headers to show tabular data properly.
· Tagging:
Adding corresponding tags for all different page elements.
· Code Cleanliness:
Removing unnecessary whitespace characters to streamline screen reader performance.
· Link Descriptions:
Adding the title property or the aria-label property to labels to describe link purposes.
· Form Validation:
Automatically detects input errors and provides correction suggestions to the user.
· Location Awareness:
Information about the user's location is available.
· Enhanced Properties:
Adding the titles property for iframes and the ALT property for images.
· Background Images:
Displaying descriptive pictures as background images.
· Tooltips:
Adding role="tooltip" for hover or focus content.
· Keyboard Operability:
Scripting to guarantee keyboard operability for a site's basic functions.
· Focus Management:
Ensuring keyboard focus can move freely on the web page.
· Accessible Naming:
Providing accessible names for forms, buttons, tags, and links.
· Component Transparency:
Disclosing information about components.
· Status Messages:
Announcing status messages for screen reader users.
Native Compliance vs. Widgets We frequently receive requests for "accessibility icons" or "widgets." Currently, the Lofty CMS does not include a built-in accessibility widget because native accessibility (like the features listed above) is superior to "overlays." Accessibility experts often criticize overlays for creating a false sense of security while failing to resolve underlying structural issues.
---
Your Responsibility: Best Practices for Content
While Lofty provides the technical framework, the content you upload must also be accessible. Customizations can impact your compliance score. Please follow these best practices to maintain a high standard of accessibility:
· Use Alt Text:
Always add descriptive alternative text to any images you upload to your website.
· Ensure Color Contrast:
When customizing your theme, use sufficient color contrast between text and background colors to ensure readability.
· Structure Content:
Use proper heading hierarchy (H1, H2, H3) to organize content logically. Do not just bold text to look like a header; use the correct heading tags.
· Provide Video Captions:
Add captions to any video content embedded on your website.
Verification & Third-Party Tools
We encourage clients to verify their own website's accessibility or use additional tools if they prefer visible compliance badges.
How to Verify Accessibility:
You can experience your website the way assistive technology users do by using the following tools:
Screen Reader Plugins:
Install browser extensions (such as the Screen Reader for Chrome) to test how your content is read aloud.
Native Screen Readers:
Use built-in tools like VoiceOver (Mac) or Narrator (Windows).
Third-Party Accessibility Widgets:
If you prefer to add a visible accessibility menu or icon to your site, the Lofty CMS supports the integration of third-party tools via our "Custom Code" feature. Popular options used by real estate professionals include:
AccessiBe (https://accessibe.com/ )
UserWay (https://userway.org/)
Note: These are third-party services. Clients are responsible for any associated costs and for verifying that the tool meets their specific compliance needs.
Audit Support
If you receive a third-party accessibility audit report, please know that many automated tests catch only about 30% of potential issues and may produce false positives.
Lofty is here to help. If you have specific findings from an audit:
Contact Support:
Send the report to our team.
Review:
We will review the findings to identify which items can be addressed through platform updates versus content adjustments you can make
We are dedicated to monitoring regulatory developments to ensure your website remains inclusive and compliant.
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your Lofty CRM.
Related terms: accessibility, ADA compliance, WCAG

#### Article 379: Cookie Preference Settings

- Article ID: `34736360933915`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `Compliance`
- Updated: `2025-11-11T02:27:02Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/34736360933915-Cookie-Preference-Settings

Introduction
If you have a Lofty website, your site visitors have the option to adjust their website cookies. Learn more about website cookies here:
Website Cookies (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/31337234468123)
. The default preference settings opts out of non-essential cookies.
Privacy laws
emphasize that
users must have clear choices
regarding data collection, particularly for advertising and tracking cookies.
Summary
How Do Cookie Settings Impact Google Analytics? (#h_01JNSEGQAF61N3GFPQVTH3FYMR)
Does This Affect Website Lead Collection and Conversion Rates? (#h_01JNSEQHS779V9WMDN20WCE4FR)
How is Lofty Addressing the Data Reduction? (#h_01JNSESQWWQAP93FEYC0P9HZ02)
Conclusion (#h_01JNSFCDP27M4D1W7G3YJ4407H)
How Do Cookie Settings Impact Google Analytics?
Based on our testing across multiple websites, implementing an opt-out default setting has resulted in the following GA data changes:
Event count decreased by approximately 40%
Total users decreased by approximately 60%
Registration data remained unaffected
This suggests:
Less meaningful traffic is filtered out
– Visitors who briefly land on your website and leave without engaging typically do not consent to cookies, so GA cannot track their activity.
Users genuinely interested in browsing your website tend to accept cookie consent
, ensuring their activity is still tracked. This is why
registration data remains stable
despite the decrease in total users and event counts.
Does This Affect Website Lead Collection and Conversion Rates?
No.
An opt-out default cookie preference
does not impact your website’s lead collection or conversion rates
. As seen in our data, registration numbers remain stable, meaning that visitors willing to engage with your business are still consenting to cookies, allowing their actions to be tracked and recorded.
How is Lofty Addressing the Data Reduction?
To mitigate data loss, we have implemented Google Consent Mode.
What Is Google Consent Mode?
Google Consent Mode allows Google Analytics and Google Ads to continue collecting anonymous modeled data, even when visitors opt out of cookies, helping to reduce data loss.
Learn more here:
Google Consent Mode (https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/10000067?hl=en)
Data Volume Requirements for Consent Mode
Google Consent Mode requires sufficient website traffic to enable effective data modeling. However, many smaller websites may not meet the required threshold. Specifically:
Google requires
at least 1,000 consented visitor interactions
(e.g., page views) to begin data modeling.
If a website has low traffic, Google may not generate modeled data, meaning opted-out user behavior will be completely absent from Google Analytics.
As a result, websites with lower traffic may see a more significant reduction in Google Analytics data.
Conclusion
Defaulting to opt-out aligns with global privacy trends and ensures compliance.
Google Analytics data will decrease, but registration data remains unchanged, indicating that interested users still opt in.
Google Consent Mode has been implemented to mitigate data loss, but its effectiveness depends on website traffic volume.
The cookie opt-out setting does not impact website lead collection or conversion rates.
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please get in touch with our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your CRM.

#### Article 380: Data Subject Access Request (DSAR)

- Article ID: `34891569535643`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `Compliance`
- Updated: `2025-11-11T02:20:05Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/34891569535643-Data-Subject-Access-Request-DSAR

Introduction
DSAR stands for Data Subject Access Request. DSAR is a request that individuals (data subjects) can make to an organization to access the personal data that the organization holds about them. DSARs are a key part of data protection laws.
The Data Subject Access Request page offers your website visitors several options to protect their data. These are outlined below.
Note:
This is currently a beta that is only available on California based websites.
Summary
Right to Opt Out of Data Sharing (#h_01JP6E0GNQXGZQZ450Y6QQYHQR)
Right to Access Their Data (#h_01JP6E7QV27WZ7PS989364KKNG)
Right to Delete Their Account (#h_01JP6EAY9F7DF29DN4QZXCGB6Z)
How will I know if my lead has made a request? (#h_01JP82KKTDP53HW07M19DE291E)
Right to Opt Out of Data Sharing
Website visitors have the right to opt out of having their data shared with any other parties. If a website visitor requests this, we will notify them that opting out of data sharing may impact their user experience when visiting your website.
If the website visitor is not logged in to the Lofty built website, they will need to opt-out again of having their data shared if they use a different device, browser, or if they clear their cookies.
If the website visitor is logged into the Lofty built website, their opt-out preference will be associated with their account. This means that they will not need to opt-out again when switching devices, browsers, or clearing cookies — their preference will be automatically applied.
Right to Access Their Data
Website visitors can request a copy of their personal data that has been collected by using your website. If this is requested, we will first verify the website visitor's email address. Upon successful verification, they will gain access to the data of the lead that is associated with their email address.
This data includes the timeline log of searches, views, favorites, and requests that they have made on your website.
Right to Delete Their Account
Website visitors have the right to request that their personal data be deleted. A ‘Delete Account’ button will be added to the website account settings, when a website visitor is logged in to your Lofty built account. Deletion requests will trigger email verification, like the ‘Right to Access’ option, to verify that the requestor is who they say they are.
When a website visitor requests to delete their account, their lead profile will be placed into the deleted pipeline. The lead will no longer receive any email or text communication. At the same time, the lead's assigned agent will be notified, informing them of the lead's request to delete their account and reminding them to manually erase the lead to meet the lead's requirements.
Lofty will not directly erase leads. It is your responsibility to fully comply with the deletion request.
How will I know if my lead has made a request?
All Data Subject Access Requests will be logged on the lead's timeline. You will also receive an email notification if action is required by you, such as a deletion request.
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please contact our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your Lofty CRM

#### Article 381: Website Cookies

- Article ID: `31337234468123`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `Compliance`
- Updated: `2025-11-11T02:27:16Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/31337234468123-Website-Cookies

Introduction
Website cookies are small text files stored on a user's device when they visit a website. This is how a website might remember your settings or history when you visit it multiple times.
A
cookie policy
is a document or section of a website that explains how cookies are used on the site. They can serve various purposes, such as improving user experience, tracking user behavior, or storing preferences.
Types of Cookies
Strictly Necessary Cookies
Strictly necessary cookies are vital for the operation of the website. These must be enabled in order for the website to load correctly.
These cookies are used to identify and authenticate users, ensure users have access to the correct site features, and maintain website security.
Performance Cookies
Performance cookies collect information about how site visitors use the website, including the pages visited and errors they encounter.
Performance cookies do not collect personal information.
These cookies are used to provide statistical information and web analytics, track affiliate links, and help improve website performance by identifying errors.
Functional Cookies
Functional cookies allow the website to remember a site visitor's preferences and provide enhanced features.
These cookies are used to remember settings like layout, text size, and language preferences, indicate if the site visitor has already participated in surveys or completed forms, and display embedded videos and other multimedia.
Targeting Cookies
Targeting cookies collect information on a site visitor's browsing habits across multiple websites.
These cookies display relevant advertisements, measure marketing campaign success, and provide personalized content recommendations.
Key Elements of a Cookie Policy
Lofty has a cookie policy both for lofty.com as well as for all websites hosted by Lofty. The cookie policy outlines the following, so all site visitors understand how their data may be collected and used.
Definition of Cookies
: Explains what cookies are and why they are used.
Types of Cookies Used
:
Essential/Strictly Necessary Cookies
: Required for the website to function (e.g., login sessions, shopping cart functionality).
Performance Cookies
: Collect data on how users interact with the site to improve performance (e.g., analytics).
Functional Cookies
: Store user preferences (e.g., language settings).
Targeting/Advertising Cookies
: Track user behavior for advertising purposes.
Purpose of Cookies
: Details how the data collected is used, such as improving user experience or delivering personalized ads.
Consent Management
: Explains how users can accept or reject cookies, often through a cookie banner or settings menu.
Third-Party Cookies
: Information about cookies placed by external services or advertisers.
Cookie Retention
: Describes how long cookies are stored on a user's device.
User Rights and Control
: Explains how users can manage or delete cookies through browser settings or opt-out mechanisms.
Why is a Cookie Policy Important?
Legal Compliance
: Many jurisdictions require websites to disclose their use of cookies and obtain user consent.
Transparency
: Builds trust with users by clearly explaining how their data is handled.
User Control
: Helps users make informed decisions about their privacy and data preferences.
Lofty manages your cookie policy, so you don't have to worry about it! Visitors to Lofty hosted website have the option to opt in or out of all cookie types, except for the strictly necessary cookies.
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please get in touch with our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your CRM.

#### Article 383: Website Template Library

- Article ID: `10486049285659`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `Custom Templates`
- Updated: `2025-11-11T09:19:14Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/10486049285659-Website-Template-Library

Introduction
This is a feature that can be made available via a Whitelist request. To request access to this feature, please contact our support team at
support@lofty.com (mailto:support@chimeinc.com)
.
This tool can control all of an account's agent website theme settings, header and footer settings, favicon, forced registration pop-up style, questionnaire style, etc.
Summary
Accessing the Template Library (#h_01GJ3V7BTFTEZTEKKFYHJR2VJF)
The Template Library (#h_01GJ3V7NA3MM83ZBYKDZJSRA1N)
Template Editor Tool (#h_01GJ3V7YTECVPG4HBM530MC57F)
Accessing the Template Library
The Website Template Library can be accessed by the Lofty Company owner or admin.
The Template Library
Lofty has created several default website templates
If a Lofty user wants to use one of these templates as is, they select it here. The user may preview the template prior to selecting it.
To create a new template, click "Add New Template".
From here, you may create a template from a website that already exists on your account:
Or, you may create a template from one of the Lofty default templates:
There is a limit of five (5) custom templates per Lofty account.
Template Editor Tool
The Template Editor is similar to the Website Editor but is simpler.
Left-side navigation has only Settings and Page Editor
The top left contains the Template Name, rather than the URL
The top right does not have options to view/preview the website
Template Settings:
Above are all the settings that can be set for a template
Within 'Permissions', when the icon is locked, the settings cannot be edited
For example, if 'Favicon' is locked, all existing sites created with this template will be synchronized to use the set Favicon.
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com> or by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557.

### Section: Customization

#### Article 384: Advanced Website Customizations

- Article ID: `360038705671`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `Customization`
- Updated: `2025-11-11T09:29:25Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360038705671-Advanced-Website-Customizations

Introduction
If you have front-end development experience and knowledge and want to get more in-depth with your website customizations, this article will provide you with the basic information you need to get started when using the Lofty CSM to do this.
There are three levels at which you can perform advanced customizations on your Lofty-built website--all of which are explained in detail in the sections below. Depending on what you want to accomplish (integrating a third-party widget, modifying a page's style, etc.), you will want to understand what is available at each level.
Notice:
The Starter package does not come with this feature. If you are on a Starter package and interested in using this feature to its full effect, please contact
Support (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/115001982346)
to get upgrade options.
Summary
Global Customizations (#h_01FGSY7KBXT85X8H3MGNYNJ9N5)
Website Currency (#h_01GDY0221ZBFCFKR2D61NZXVV5)
Page Customizations (#h_01FGSY8Y3VAZK2CHCCD7CX4PGG)
Block Customizations (#h_01FGSY91JJY0NSTMJSSG1D9T05)
Global Customizations
To establish global customizations on your Lofty-built website, navigate to the
CMS
>
Settings
>
Tools
. You should be able to
click here (https://cms.lofty.com/cmsnew/setting?sp=customCode)
to get there as well (assuming you are signed in).
This type of customization is divided into two different areas: (a) styles and (b) scripts--both of which are explained in more detail in their corresponding section below.
(a) Global Styles
Styles influence a page's layout, structure, color, shape, etc. Scripts can greatly enhance the visual aspects of static web pages.
Add
document.head
to the link tag embedded.
Write style directly. For example, use
h1{color:red;}
rather than
<style>h1{color:red;}<style>
.
(b) Global Scripts
An example of when you might use scripts is if you need to embed a piece of code to track your site's conversion.
Run the
new Function('siteAppVm', customcode.script)(siteAppVm)
each time you enter the page. This can be used as an immediate function.
The script content is the function body
The properties defined in the function body are not globally accessible
The function parameter is siteAppVm (explained in the global object)
For example, to globally define a method
foo()
that fires when a button is clicked, you would do the following.
Custom Style & Script / Script:
window.foo(){
console.log('hello, world')
}
Button to trigger:
<a href="javascript:foo();">WELCOME!</a>
Global Object
(1) siteAppVm
SiteAppVm is a Vue instance mounted on the
document.querySelector('main.page-content')
element.
moduleData
ModuleData is an array
[{name: module 1,data:{}},{name: module 2,data:{}}]
. Objects are modules on the page in the array. Modules are displayed from top to bottom on the page. Depending on the dynamic binding technology, you can modify the moduleData in the moduleData to modify the content display of the module.
// Suppose siteAppvm. moduleData[0] is a header module
// Change the size of the logo to 300
siteAppVm.moduleData[0].data.size = 300
(2) Util
(a) addStyle(css, async=true)
Function
: Add link tag in
document.head
Usage
:
Util.addStyle(css:String, async:Boolean)
Parameters
:
CSS:
If the CSS string contains '.css', then regard it as a link. For example:
Util.addStyle("//static.chimeroi.com/servicetool-temp/example.css", true)
Or the CSS string refers to the content of the style like this:
Util.addStyle(".red{color:red;}", true)
Async:
- True: This means that the return of the
Util.addStyle()
the function is Promise, which means the CSS code has been completely loaded on this page.
- False: This means that the return of the
Util.addStyle()
function is a link element that loads the CSS code in the document.
(a) Example
: How to introduce a Google font link: https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Sofia
Because this is a link without '.css', then a '&name=sofia.css' suffix needs to be used to let Util.addStyle() function by regarding it as a link.
Util.addStyle("https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Sofia&name=sofia.css")
(b) addScript(url, async = true)
Function
: Add script code in
document.body
Usage
:
Util.addScript(url: String, async: Boolean)
Parameters
:
URL:
A link to the script page
Async:
- True: This means that the return of the
Util.addScript()
function is Promise, which means the JavaScript has been completely loaded. If the script was cached, then it will use cache.
- False: This means that it will insert the external link script in <head> instead of using cache.
(b) Example
: Run certain functions after some JavaScript has been loaded completely.
Util.addScript('//www.example.com/1.js').then(_=>foo())
It is necessary to run the script again each time a new page is reached instead of using the cache. Suppose the content of this link https://www.example.com/1.js is as follows:
console.log('welcom to visit', location.pathname)
The control center needs to publish the path of the current page each time it is reached.
Util.addScript('//www.example.com/1.js', false)
(c) toast(text, delay = 1000)
Usage
:
Util.toast(text:String, delay: Number)
Example
:
Util.toast('hello', delay: 2000)
. With this function, a hint of 'hello' will show on the current page and disappear two seconds later.
(d) isMobileSize(size = 600)
Usage
:
Util.isMobileSize(Number)
Example
:
Util.isMobileSize(700)
. Used to determine whether the screen width is less than 700px.
(e) Util.login(options)
Function
: Pop up a login box
Attributes in options
:
Attributes
Type
Function
allowClose
Boolean
Whether a close button is permitted
showFacebook
Boolean
Whether to allow the site visitor to log in with a Facebook account or not
showGoogle
Boolean
Whether to allow the site visitor to log in with a Google account or not
Example
: Pop up the login box
with
a close button.
Util.login({allowClose: true})
(f) Util.register(options)
Function
: Pop up a registration box
Attributes in options
:
Attributes
Type
Function
allowClose
Boolean
Whether a close button is permitted
showFacebook
Boolean
Whether to allow the site visitor to register with  a Facebook account or not
showGoogle
Boolean
Whether to allow the site visitor to register with a Google account or not
Example
: Pop up the forced registration box
without
a close button and using a Google account to register is
not
allowed.
Util.login({allowClose: false, showGoogle: false})
(3) siteAxios
The siteAxios points to the module [axios](https://github.com/axios/axios).
Using the axios module to intercept a request and modify the request parameters:
// Add a request interceptor
window.siteAxios.interceptors.request.use(
function (config) {
// Do something before request is sent
return config;
},
function (error) {
// Do something with request error
return Promise.reject(error);
}
);
Using the axios module to intercept a response and modify the response data:
// Add a response interceptor
window.siteAxios.interceptors.response.use(
function (response) {
// Any status code that lie within the range of 2xx cause this function to trigger
// Do something with response data
// For example:
var config = response.__config__;
var addHouse = /api-site\/sell\add-house/;
var register = /api-site\/leadRegister;
if (config && (register.test(configurl) || addHouse.test(config.url))) {
debugger
}
return response;
},
function (error) {
// Any status codes that falls outside the range of 2xx cause this function to trigger
// Do something with response error
return Promise.reject(error);
}
);
Website Currency
This setting allows Lofty users to change the default currencies on their Lofty websites. Visitors to these websites can also change the currency displayed.
To access this setting, navigate to
CMS -> Tools -> Language/Currency
. There is an option to sync currencies to agent subdomains, but subdomains
cannot
set their own currencies.
We currently support the following currencies:
US Dollar
Canadian Dollar
Euro
Pound Sterling
Chinese Yuan
Japanese Yen
Visitors to the website can easily change the currency:
The currency will change in the following sections:
Listing/Sold prices
Home Valuation
values
Mortgage Calculator
Page Customizations
To establish global customizations on your Lofty-built website, first navigate to the
CMS
>
Page Editor
>
Pages
:
Once you have clicked on
Pages
, select the setting wheel for the page you would like to add customize to. The screenshot below shows the
Home Page
being selected, but you can choose the page that you want to apply the customization to.
Then, scroll down and select the drop-down menu for
Page Style & Script
:
This type of customization is also divided into two different areas: (a) styles and (b) scripts. Both are explained below.
(a) Page Styles
Page styles influence the current page's layout, structure, color, shape, etc.
The page style will only apply to the current page. You can add it to the page by using
Util.addStyle(pageStyle, false)
.
Write style directly. For example, use
h1{color:red;}
rather than
<style>h1{color:red;}<style>
.
(b) Page Scripts
Page scripts can significantly enhance the current static page. You may consider using page scripts when you need to embed a script to track certain conversion data on the current page.
Page scripts will only run on the current page. Similar to what is outlined above for
Global Scripts (#h_01FGSZR2TA9N0B596QVXSAJKEN)
, the page scripts also run by using
new Function(pageScript).call(siteAppVm)
. But the 'this' pointer points to siteAppVm.
Block Customizations
There are two block types available in the Lofty CMS that can be utilized to embed custom code. Please reference the two articles below to learn more:
Content Block (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360038611351)
Code Block (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/4407612265499)
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your Lofty CRM.
Related term: custom style, custom script

### Section: Featured Area

#### Article 386: Add / Edit Featured Areas

- Article ID: `360037816512`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `Featured Area`
- Updated: `2026-04-15T17:38:40Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360037816512-Add-Edit-Featured-Areas

Introduction
Lofty supports creating a landing page to feature each area in your market to attract more leads using auto-populated local information. Different featured area pages have the same style with content related to that area. Creating them one by one could be a lot of work, so the CMS Tool also supports simultaneously creating a group of featured area pages.
Summary
Add a Featured Area (#h_01G3HR6GCHJA28ED0TYG2VGEHW)
Add a Featured Area Page to your Website (#h_01GC9WBK0S6JGT9R9K8234P66R)
Edit a Featured Area Page (#h_01GC9WBSB22KT3NN16516FCRZW)
Add a Featured Area
Navigate to the CMS and select
Areas
.
Click the
+ Add New Area
button and pick
City
or
Neighborhood
.
The cities and neighborhoods available are dependent on the connected MLSs. Use the search bar to type in the area you want to add.
Select the Agent who represents this area.
Featured Area Pages
After the city/neighborhood has been added, 2-3 pages will be created.
Introduction Page
The Introduction page includes a description of the area, market trends, current listings, amenities and attractions, schools and demographics.
Note:
If the region selected lacks data, the Introduction will not be displayed.
Search Page
The Search page lists the homes for sale in the selected area and market insights.
Market Page
The Market page provides a market snapshot, market trends, and recent listings.
Add a Featured Area Page to your Website
Navigate to the Page Editor and click on the
Pages
option.
Click the
+ Add Page
button and select the
Featured Area
page template.
Select a style and click
Next
. Locate the area you want to add using the search bar and choose it by clicking the box next to it. You can also click the top box to select all areas.
The introductory page navigation for any areas you have chosen and saved will display under
Page Editor>Pages>Hidden Navigation
and can be personalized like other pages.
To display the area in the navigation bar menu, hover over the box corresponding to the area, click, and hold while moving the pointer to the related folder like "Neighborhoods".
After completing the rest of the configuration, don't forget to click the "Publish" button in the top-right of the CMS Tool for the changes to apply to the live website.
Edit a Featured Area Page
If you want to adjust the page style, please refer to
Add / Remove / Edit Blocks on Pages (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360037816532)
.
*IMPORTANT
: Please note that if you edit a Featured Area page group, your modifications will apply to all Featured Areas in this group at the same time.
If you want to modify the content for the pages you just configured, you can click the
Edit
option next to the Featured Area that you want to edit.
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please contact our Support Team via email at support@lofty.com, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat through your Lofty CRM.
Related terms: Featured Area, Featured Areas Page

### Section: Header/Footer/Logo

#### Article 388: Footer

- Article ID: `360038293211`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `Header/Footer/Logo`
- Updated: `2025-11-11T02:29:46Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360038293211-Footer

Introduction
The footer is a very important part of any website as it presents more company information, contact details, links to sites on the page, important MLS disclaimers, etc. Having this section up-to-date and ready to go is going to be an important part of building your Lofty website.
*Keep in mind that just like the website header, the footer can only be edited on the Home page via the CMS Tool. The steps to adjust this are found in this article.
There are four different styles to the footer. They will vary slightly with how the content is laid out and some of them might have two different background colors, etc.:
Summary
Edit Website Footer (#h_01GZ4BYGAYHBYF9NGQNT8R7CWR)
Removing or Hiding the Footer (#h_01GZ4BYSQQBMS6X279F44CFJ9W)
Edit Website Footer
On the Page Editor, navigate to the home page, scroll to the bottom of the home page, and double-click on the footer block or click on the "Edit" icon in the top-right of the footer block.
To change the style, scroll all the way to the bottom of the footer settings and select the button to "Change Style":
You can adjust the background color(s) in the "Footer Background" section of the footer settings:
Make any changes to the "Sitemap Menu Style" including font weight, font size, font color, and hover color:
If there are any drop-down menus on your site navigation, you will need to adjust them here:
One of the most important parts of the footer is going to be the display of any logos. Currently, you can upload up to five logos on the footer. You can also define the "alt text" and URL (when clicked) for each logo. If you want to change the order of the logos, just drag and drop using the option on the right side of each logo.
Choose the "agent" whose information (name, phone, email, address) should be displayed in the footer. That information is set up in
CMS Tool
>
Settings
>
Team Info
>
Creator/Agent
.
If you are an Enterprise owner or an Enterpriser user with a Manage Website permission, there is an option to display either the company
name
or
group name
or to customize the displayed content. The dropdown menu will display the company name and all the upper-level groups' names.
There is also an option to add custom content to a Lofty website footer. This is available on any editable Lofty website.
The content added here will sync to any subdomains that are created off of this Lofty website.
This feature allows you to add extra phone numbers, addresses, or other agent/office information.
Adjust the "Agent Name Style," "Agent Phone Style," "Agent Email Style," "Company Name Style," and "Company Address Style." All of these settings will include Font Weight, Font Size, and Font Color as seen here:
You can also add your own disclaimers to your footer by inputting any text or external links. Up to five disclaimers can be added to the footer. The disclaimers will be displayed under the agent info when using styles 1, 2, or 3 and under the sitemap when using style 4.
Removing or Hiding the Footer
For some pages, you might want to keep the footer from appearing in order to keep site visitors focused on the content of the page and avoid giving them access to additional content right away.
*IMPORTANT
: With the footer, you need to be careful about when to hide it because it could take you out of compliance with your MLS.
In order to remove or hide the footer, you will want to access the page editor and then select "Pages" in the top-left:
You will then select the "cog wheel" edit icon next to the page where you want to adjust this setting.
You will then be able to edit the setting for "Page Style" where you can choose whether the header and footer display or maybe just one or the other.
FAQ
Q:
Can I remove t
he copyright language "
Made in Phoenix, AZ by your friends at
Lofty Technologies (https://chime.me/)
, Inc. Copyright 2023 All Rights Reserved." on my account owner site?
A:
Yes, please reach out to our
Support Team via email at
<support@lofty.com (mailto:%3Csupport@chimeinc.com)
>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chatting with us through your Lofty CRM.
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at
<support@lofty.com (mailto:%3Csupport@chimeinc.com)
>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by a chat with us through your Lofty CRM.
Related terms: site footer, copyright, footer information, custom content

#### Article 389: Header

- Article ID: `360054747512`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `Header/Footer/Logo`
- Updated: `2025-12-11T00:24:26Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360054747512-Header

Introduction
The header is a very important part of any website, especially because it contains the navigation linking to all other pages on your site (and potentially external sites as well). The style of the header can be edited via the CMS by following the steps in this article.
Summary
Where to Edit the Header (#h_01EYC7GVT3D8Q17BBWW76T7VK8)
Style (#h_01EYC7H163MZY408D5RESX7JYC)
Other Style Settings (#h_01EYC7H8WYNT3AEDA19QJG8PWC)
Text Style (#h_01EYC7HHCCYGK4SA9QJSDGTC5P)
Header Content (#h_01EYC7HRHGKN2ATC9DVV85KDB2)
Hiding the Header (#h_01EYC7HXGGK0H4T047BE82XWE6)
Where to Edit the Header
There is only one location where you can actually edit the website header. Navigate to the
CMS
>
Page Editor
>
Home Page
>
Selected Header
>
Edit
:
*IMPORTANT
: The header can only be edited on the Home page, not on any other pages.
Style
To edit the style, click on the "Change Style" button after having selected the header:
Header Styles
You will then choose from the seven available header styles
Style 1
Style 2
Style 3
Style 4
Style 5
Style 6
Style 7
This style is unique because the logos are centered, with the navigation split on both sides. Any navigation links that cannot fit on the left side of the logo will be available on the right side if there is space. If there is no space, it will collapse them into the drop-down menu.
When viewed on a mobile device, the logo will be centered as long as it is only one logo:
However, if you upload two logos to the header, they will be aligned to the left:
Other Style Settings
Header Background
Choose the color and transparency level with this setting here:
Secondary Menu Background
This secondary menu background color can be adjusted here:
This "secondary menu" refers to the menu that appears when opening a folder on the menu, like so (green):
Text Style
Menu Text Weight, Font Size, Text Color
Adjust these settings here:
Secondary Menu and Hover Text Color
Adjust with these settings here:
These settings apply to the secondary menu, as you can see in this screenshot here:
Overlap Style & Sticky Navigation
You can choose whether to use an "overlap style" or not for the header. This style will be overlapped with the block just under the header (typically the
Hero Block (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360038293231)
), so adjusting the opacity of the header background color might contribute to a better visual experience overall. Note that the adjustments set for opacity only work when the site visitor is at the top of the page. When scrolling down, the opacity will be at 100%.
"Sticky Navigation" refers to whether you would like to have the navigation menu (header) scroll down with the site visitor or if you would like to have it stay at the top. If you would like to have the menu scroll down with the site visitor, turn this setting ON.
Header Content
To adjust the header content, click on the
Content
tab at the top of the header settings:
On this page, you can configure the following:
Logo1
Logo2
Alt Text
Logo Size
Logo Link
This setting is available if you would like to redirect your site visitors to somewhere other than the home page when they click on the logo. The default is set to be the home page (displayed as "/") so no configuration is required if that is acceptable. In order for it to redirect a site visit to an external site, be sure "http://" or "https://" is included. For an internal site, just grab the first part after the .com. For example, for the About page on your website, you would add "/about" in the "Logo Link" field.
Agent Info (if using Header
Style 5 (#h_01EYC77705AJ5TMQNAKSWV353X)
)
Note: The file size limit is 50 MB; 100 px is also a good size. We
also support squares, but the system will compress or crop if the aspect ratio is too large; the most suitable ratio is 3:2.
Hiding the Header
*IMPORTANT
: In many situations, removing or hiding the Header is not advisable as it contains your branding information (logo, etc.) that an MLS will require to be present when displaying listings on your website. You will want to make sure that there are no issues with MLS compliance before hiding the website header.
If you do want to remove or hide the header, exit the header configuration and then click on
Pages
in the top-left of the
Page Editor
:
You will then select the "cog wheel" edit icon next to the page where you want to adjust this setting. This is edited at a page-by-page level, so if you hide on one page, it will not be hidden on the others unless configured one by one to do so.
You will then be able to edit the setting for "Page Style," where you can choose whether the header and footer display, or maybe just one or the other.
Here is an example of what the "Simple Header" looks like. It only shows the logo, agent image, agent contact information, and license ID.
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com> or by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557.

#### Article 390: Logo

- Article ID: `29525747357851`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `Header/Footer/Logo`
- Updated: `2025-11-11T02:29:01Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/29525747357851-Logo

Introduction
Your logo represents your company's brand. It is typically displayed in the header or top area of a website and serves as a quick and recognizable identifier for visitors. Clicking the logo will bring website visitors back to your home page.
When uploading your logo to your Lofty website, we recommend using a .png file that is 96 pixels in height.
Generally, a logo that is twice as wide as it is tall works best.
Uploading a Logo
To upload your website logo, navigate to the website editor, edit the header, and click the edit icon to upload your logo.
The logo location will vary depending on the style of your header. You may add up to two (2) logos.
Scroll down to the footer to add your logo there.
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please contact our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

### Section: Home Valuation

#### Article 391: Home Valuation Block

- Article ID: `360037923112`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `Home Valuation`
- Updated: `2025-11-11T03:19:31Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360037923112-Home-Valuation-Block

Introduction
The "Home Valuation" block is a very useful tool for capturing seller leads on real estate websites. It will attract potential home sellers by giving them a free home valuation estimate for their property.
Note: If you are located in Canada, please see
Feature Availability for Users in Canada (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360056581812)
There are two styles for this block that only vary in small details. On both, it will take two steps to capture the seller lead's contact information and home address and the third step will show the home valuation estimate to the lead.
Here are what the two styles look like:
Add the Home Valuation Block
Editing the Home Valuation Block
STEP 1
The site visitor will input their home address into the address box (they can choose from the Google address suggestions) and then click the button to the next step. In order to attract potential sellers and improve the conversion rate, you can edit the title and description that are shown at the top of the page. You can also change the background image(s)--this can be just one single image or multiple images (slideshow).
As for the button and search box style, you can adjust the button text and its style and change the color of the search box border. In addition, the placeholder text in the search box can also be edited, the default will be "Enter your street address."
STEP 2
After submitting the address, the visitor is required to provide their contact info to view the home valuation estimate for their property. Here is that step:
The title and description of the right side can be edited and you can choose your preferred name format (full name or first and last name) and whether the name and phone are required. You can also assign an agent that is active on your agent roster as well.
*Please note that the email is required and cannot be changed to optional. The color of the "Next" button can be adjusted as well.
STEP 3
When the lead completes the previous step (#2), a home valuation report will be sent to their email and an estimated price of the address will be shown on the screen. Here is what that looks like:
You can edit the background color of this final set of data:
Lofty uses
Bridge API (https://www.bridgeinteractive.com/resources/api-documentation/)
(a company owned by Zillow) data to give the estimated price. If you do not believe that this price is accurate enough to show to your lead, you can choose "No" under the setting for Auto Home Valuation.
If "No" is selected, the following will display and then the agent can reach out to provide a more accurate estimate with their industry experience and available resources.
Home Evaluation Report
After requesting a home evaluation via this feature, site visitors will receive an email that looks like the following (assuming the option to provide the home value is selected):
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

#### Article 392: Home Valuation Page

- Article ID: `360038509091`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `Home Valuation`
- Updated: `2025-11-11T03:19:21Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360038509091-Home-Valuation-Page

Introduction
The "Home Evaluation Page" is the default page used for capturing seller leads. When a website visitor completes this form, they will automatically receive a free home evaluation report email after they provide their address and contact information. Here is an example of what this page looks like:
Summary
Add a Home Evaluation Page (#h_01HC24VA7G0G1ZPPFQ99XX4PXR)
Home Evaluation Report (#h_01HC24VA7GJGTTFA503SNDQNGJ)
Home Evaluation Logic (#h_01HZNAHHVCPP7VDZ2TV6MZ0ZB4)
Add a Home Evaluation Page
One of these pages is built into the website by default, but if you want to add additional home evaluation pages, do the following.
Click on "Pages" from the Page Editor:
Click on "+ Add Page"
Select "Home Evaluation" from the page template list, select the style, and click "Next":
Reference the
Home Evaluation Block (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360037923112)
to learn about the settings that can be adjusted with the Home Evaluation block.
Reference
Add / Edit Website Pages (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360037816472)
to learn about editing a page's basic settings and SEO.
If you want to promote this page on social media or other marketing channels, Lofty recommends changing the "Page Style" to "With simple header" or "No header," to make sure the site visitors are focused on the Home Evaluation content and are not distracted by other pages that would otherwise be visible in the header navigation.
Home Evaluation Report
After requesting a home evaluation via this feature, site visitors will receive an email that looks like the following (assuming the option to provide the home value is selected):
The Home Evaluation Report will include the following information about the lead's property:
The estimated home value
The estimated high value
The estimated low value
The price change in the last 30 days
Home Evaluation Logic
The home value estimation given via the Home Evaluation form is provided by a third-party provider. The report cannot be edited. We recommend utilizing the CMA tool to provide a customized Home Evaluation report to a lead. Learn more about Lofty's CMA tool here:
How to Create a CMA Report (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/26265328610075)
If a lead provides a Canadian address, they will not automatically receive a home value estimation. Instead, they will receive a message similar to the one below, letting the lead know that an agent will be reaching out.
The lead's address and contact information will be captured, so that you can provide an accurate home evaluation and other relevant details directly.
FAQ
Q: Who is the source of our Home Valuation data in the Lofty sites?
A: Lofty uses
Bridge API (https://www.bridgeinteractive.com/resources/api-documentation/)
(a company owned by Zillow) data to give the estimated price.
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your Lofty CRM.
