Introduction
The "Form Block" allows you to embed a contact form (and custom fields) in specific parts of your website where you choose to put the block. The instructions for setting this block up are found below.
Summary
Adding the Form Block (#h_01F8RC3T4FYBXHRN5S92DDBRD0)
Form Types (#h_01F8RC3XTAVM5TB5R9BEVR6BHA)
(1) Contact Form (#h_01F8RC43K6MXEH85DGJQYAYZA1)
(2) Sell Form (#h_01F8RC46N9Q20GQVP1DZBN8QYF)
(3) Other Form (#h_01F8RC4A1KY6C4PVWXQH9JDBZK)
Form Settings (#h_01F8RCQKHBXE8NM2EN5NRN858F)
Lead Type (#h_01F8RE58V7B6QT8R32B8ZNK02M)
Tag (#h_01F8RE5EGC145F1RAHWHSKZKAQ)
Form Questions (#h_01F8RE5KQJAK6AG3P6JDKNXT25)
Email (#h_01F8RE5RP5S04XWNXSBFTDABWA)
Name (#h_01F8RE5X9TNAXWS5ND9PDR8X9C)
Phone (#h_01F8RE626Z4G6H1FDVXTVBE5TS)
Address (#h_01F8RE6742MKETN7GZM5JVQSZF)
Message (#h_01F8RE6BG2WD9C2EWFP9M3Y5D1)
Date (#h_01F8RE6GM79XXEECWZ99V0H8TE)
Single Line Text (#h_01F8RE6MASJ7X6WKJE96EH7XRJ)
Paragraph Text (#h_01F8RE6S50KMGTQKW0832XFJ95)
Button (#h_01F8RE6ZBZRWDM4YNH95FA8GAP)
Adding the Form Block
To add the Form Block, navigate to
CMS
>
Page Editor
>
+ Blocks
:
Choose
Form
, select the style that you would like to add to your page, and then drag it to the right side:
Form Types
There are three types of form blocks available in the Block Library. A sample of each style is outlined below:
(1) Contact Form
This is the typical contact form that you would see displayed on your website. This type of form also presents the agent profile with their contact information, etc. There are many options for this style of the Form Block, but typically they will look like the following:
(2) Sell Form
This form, when submitted, triggers a request from the site visitor/lead to sell their home. There are a variety of form styles that use this option, but typically they will look like the following:
(3) Other Form
The "Other Form" is simple and does not have the agent info displayed. Here is what that form typically looks like:
Form Settings
In general, the following are the settings that should be available whenever you edit a Form Block.
Lead Type
Choose the lead type that will be assigned to any new leads that are captured via this form. The following are options:
Buyer
Seller
Renter
Investor
Agent
Homeowner
Landlord
Other
Agent Type Lead
Since agent-type leads are individuals looking for work and only need the ability to leave messages without needing to experience other site features, so we allow you to submit information through forms without login, and the message will still be displayed in the CRM.
When you attempt to log in or use features that require logging in, such as "save search," there will be a relevant prompt.
The lead ownership configuration in the landing page will also be aligned with the CRM. In addition to being able to select Personal and Company, it will also be able to choose a specific office where the site owner belongs.
Tag
Choose tags that will be applied to any leads that complete this form. Use these tags to categorize your leads, trigger automation with Smart Plans, etc.
Note that this feature also works for existing leads. If an existing lead fills out the form on the website that has been edited to include tags, those tags will be added to the existing lead's profile.
Form Questions
Though there are a few exceptions within the different form styles (sell my home, for example), for the most part, most of the questions used within the Form Block can be customized to fit your needs and capture the information that you are looking for from site visitors on your site. Currently, there is no limit to the number of questions that can be added to a form. All responses to form questions will feed into the lead's profile page in the CRM and an email will be sent to you as the Lofty user.
There are two categories for form questions:
Built-In Fields
(can only be added once)
Email
Name
Phone
Address
Message
Date
Additional Fields
(can be added multiple times)
Single Line Text
Paragraph Text
Email
This is required for every form.
Name
You can choose "Full Name" or "First and Last Name" format. You can also set this field as required or optional.
Phone
The phone number for the site visitor. Can be set as required.
Address
First, choose the address type.
Individual Address: just one address input field and a Google address suggestion will be given when the site visitor inputs an address
Full Address: This is divided into four separate fields (Street Address, City, State, and Zip Code). There will be no Google address suggestions with the "Full Address" type selected.
You can set this field as required or optional.
If the visitor submits this field on your form, there will be a property generated and associated with the lead’s profile page on the CRM:
Message
You can customize the "Field Label" (the field name displayed on the form). You can also set this field as required or optional. If the site visitor submits this field on your form, there will be a "_________ left a message" log generated on the timeline of the lead’s profile page. It will also trigger a notification to the primary agent associated with the lead.
Date
This field will let the site visitor choose a date in the form using a calendar picker. You can customize the "Field Label" (the field name displayed on the form) as you want. Also, you can set this field as required or optional. The date info will be recorded
as a note
in the lead’s profile page of the CRM.
Single Line Text
Create a new field that you can name. This field is intended for a small response from the site visitor. You can make it optional or required.
Paragraph Text
Create a new field that you can name. This larger paragraph text field is intended for larger responses from the site visitor. Optional/required can also be toggled on or off.
Button
With this setting, you can choose to display a "Thank You Message"
or
to redirect the visitor to a specific URL. If you choose "Thank You Message," you can choose the message that the site visitor will see after submitting the form. If you choose the URL, you can input the URL that the visitor will be redirected to after submission of the form.
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by a chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

#### Article 431: Questionnaire Settings

- Article ID: `360038005412`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `Registration Setting`
- Updated: `2025-11-11T03:22:13Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360038005412-Questionnaire-Settings

Introduction
The "Questionnaire" whose settings you can adjust consists of the questions asked of a lead
after
they already provide their information. With "Questionnaire Settings," you can edit whether the questions will appear, whether they can be skipped, and then the style. You can also customize the questions that will appear.
For context, the questions asked of a lead
after
they register consist of the following:
Buyer
Are you a first-time home buyer?
Within how many months do you plan to buy a home?
Have you been pre-qualified for a mortgage?
Do you have a house to sell first?
Are you already working with an agent?
Seller
Within how many months do you plan to sell a home?
Is there a mortgage on your house now?
Do you want to buy a house?
Do you have an agent already?
More information regarding the prior step to this questionnaire (registration pop-up) can be found in these two articles:
Registration Pop-up Trigger Rule (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360038373331)
and
Registration Pop-up Style (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360056629652)
.
Summary
Edit Questionnaire Settings (#h_01GYJF6TE0RQ4CPDK3M4BJP62J)
Customize Questions (#h_01GYJF727S4HKGRDS9QAQMGX27)
Edit Questionnaire Settings
To access the settings, click on the "
Settings
" icon on the left menu when in the CMS Tool, select "
Lead Capture
," and finally "
Questionnaire Settings
."
Note that there are technically two forms: (1) Buyer and (2) Seller. Each has its settings, though they are the same settings that can be adjusted. Click on the tab for the one that you want to edit:
Choose whether you want to have this questionnaire appear or not (remember this would have to be turned off for both buyer and seller separately). You can also choose whether you want to allow leads to close the form with an "x" that will be in the top-right:
You can then edit the background color, title, description, and button text for both forms. Please note that the button color will use the global button color set in the Style Settings of the Page Editor.
Customize Questions
To customize the questions, you can click on the options to edit, drag/drop to reorder, and the "eyeball" icon to hide. The contents of all custom questions will be added to the lead's profile in the CRM as a note.
When editing a question, it will look like this:

the
Registration Pop-up Trigger Rule (https://help.chime.me/hc/en-us/articles/360038373331)
.

Settings Location

CMS
(website editor) >
Lead Capture
>

:
Style
There are three different styles that can be used and the content settings will vary depending on the style selected. Choose the style right at the top:
Single Column
Two Columns
One Step Column
Content
If you choose either the "Single Column" or the "Two Columns" style, you will be presented with two different steps where you will need to configure the content:
If you choose the "One Step Column," you will only have to configure the content for that one step.
To configure the content, simply complete the fields which include the following:
Background Color
Title
Description
Button Text
Thank you Message
Registration Settings
Here you will edit whether you will set the name and phone number as "Required" or "Optional." Please note that email is always going to be marked as required.
Please note that the configuration of this setting can affect Google Chrome One-Click Website Registration. For more information on this topic, please reference the following article:
Google Chrome One-Click Website Registration (https://help.chime.me/hc/en-us/articles/360055890631)
.
Add Third-Party Registration
In order for these options to be available, a manual configuration by the Lofty Support Team will have to take place when your website is set up. This is built into the onboarding and account creation process, but if you do not see these options for some reason, please reach out to the Lofty Support Team for further assistance (
support@lofty.com (mailto:support@chimeinc.com)
).
Please note that in order to use the "Google Chrome One-Click Website Registration" you will need to have the "Google" box checked and enabled on your forced registration. For more information on this topic, please reference the following article:
Google Chrome One-Click Website Registration (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360055890631)
.
Email-Only Lead Registration
Registration Logic (#id-3/4/2021:FeatureReleaseTrainingforCRM3.21,Site5.9-RegistrationLogic)
Turn On/Off (#h_01F54918R0YW9KC6G98ERZ1254)
Additional Info (#h_01F5491C03CC2S8FWDMP3AYEB8)
Return to Site Logic (#id-3/4/2021:FeatureReleaseTrainingforCRM3.21,Site5.9-ReturntoSiteLogic)
Registration Logic
A specific logic has been built into the registration pop-up on certain registration styles for your website. This logic is designed to capture email addresses during the registration process, even if the site visitor did not provide all of their information (name, phone).
If a lead provides at least their email address but backs out of the full registration process before providing their name and phone number, you will capture an email-only lead after a five-minute built-in delay.
This is only supported in the following scenarios:
When a lead fills out their email address in the built-in field of the
Single Column (#h_01EYC48C3YBNP6XHCC5W80G0CT)
registration style but does not provide their name or phone number in the second step.
When a lead fills out their email address in the built-in field of the
Two Columns (#h_01EYC48F95SA2H7HXHR0V85Q8P)
registration style but does not provide their name or phone number in the second step.
When a lead clicks on the
Continue with Facebook
or
Continue with Gmail
button on any of the registration styles. When they do so, they will be asked to provide their phone number. If they back out of the process before providing their phone number, their email address will be captured.
Turn On/Off
If you would like to turn this feature on/off, you can now navigate to
CMS
>
Settings
>
Lead Capture
>
Site
Email Lead
and toggle this feature on/off. It will be
enabled
by default.
Additional Info
It is very important that you are aware of the following information:
If no name is captured the lead will be saved as "No Name" in your CRM
Leads captured via this method will maintain their original source depending on how they found your website. They were
previously
saved as the lead source of "Site Email Lead" but that logic was discontinued on May 8, 2021.
Leads captured will all be tagged with a
private tag
called "Lofty Email Lead" so that you can easily filter by these specific leads in the future.
By default, these leads are considered as "opted-out" which means auto email communication can not be sent to them until they are opted-in. See
Email Opt-In Status for more information (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/4403048145307)
.
If you plan to market to these leads, please make sure you are aware of how they entered your system. They did not finish the registration process but they did type in their email address and continued to the next step before backing out (and not providing name/phone).
Return to Site Logic
If a site visitor had previously provided their email address but did not finalize registration, the next time they are on your Lofty-built site, they will be prompted to provide their phone number to finalize registration. This same pop-up will appear one time per day until they provide a phone number.
Questions?

#### Article 434: User Consent Disclaimer

- Article ID: `27710855547547`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `Registration Setting`
- Updated: `2025-11-11T03:21:53Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/27710855547547-User-Consent-Disclaimer

Introduction
When a lead registers on your website, it is important to capture their consent to be contacted by you. This article shows how to customize the disclaimer that a lead will see when they register on your Lofty IDX site.
Adding the Disclaimer
By default, your IDX website will have a checkbox with a disclaimer that lets a lead know that by registering on your website, they are consenting to be contacted by you. Per 10DLC and TCPA regulations, you must capture this consent to contact leads via text or phone call. If you do not edit the disclaimer, it will look like this:
The box will need to be checked in order to complete registration and import the lead details to your CRM. This keeps you compliant and leads are aware that they may be contacted by you soon!
You cannot edit this disclaimer, but you can add additional disclaimers by navigating to
Website > Settings > Lead Capture > Disclaimer
. Click
+ Add a new disclaimer under the Custom Disclaimer section
to open a text box that will replace the default language on the registration pop-up.
Up to three (3) disclaimers can be added. Each disclaimer will have a checkbox that must be checked to submit registration.
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your CRM.

#### Article 435: Enhancing Real Estate SEO through Strategic Backlink Building

- Article ID: `27854941981467`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `SEO Best Practices`
- Updated: `2025-11-11T03:09:14Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/27854941981467-Enhancing-Real-Estate-SEO-through-Strategic-Backlink-Building

Introduction
This guide explores the significance of backlinks in SEO, providing real estate professionals with actionable strategies to improve their online visibility and search engine rankings.
Summary
What are Backlinks (#h_01J42WNZ50SPR3081Z2J4J19X7)
Understanding the Importance of Backlinks (#h_01J42WRJ01GZSFS995DRB3KSY6)
Strategies for Building Backlinks (#h_01J42WVMPY16N9GBMAYWF7B32A)
Building Backlinks with Local Citations (#h_01J42WVWBBQRBVCXZDYCTMT16D)
Link Building on Social Media (#h_01J42X5SW8A0ZP35D7TRWJY24H)
Consistent Content Creation (#h_01J42XAFCNS3FH2Y1070BA5YMK)
Establishing Yourself as the Local Real Estate Expert: Building Trust and Backlinks (#h_01J42XEVC1QX4V69BM0XKSD984)
What are Backlinks
Backlinks are links from one website to another, acting as endorsements that affirm the credibility and relevance of your content to search engines such as Google. Backlinks are essential to SEO.
A top-tier backlink typically comes from a respected site within the same or a related industry, greatly enhancing the search engine ranking of the linked site.
The greater the number of high-quality backlinks from pertinent sources like real estate websites, news outlets, or local directories, the better your website's ranking in search results for local homebuyers and sellers. This results in heightened online visibility, drawing more qualified leads and ultimately expanding your real estate business.
Understanding the Importance of Backlinks
Backlinks are a major piece of the SEO (search engine optimization) puzzle.  You need one to complement and elevate the other.
High-level, here are some quick reasons why it’s important to have a good backlink strategy:
Backlinks are how Google (and other search engines) discover your pages.
They demonstrate to Google that your website has a trustworthy reputation, which encourages search engines to direct users to reliable sites.
Relevant backlinks can enhance your website's authority within your industry or niche.
Backlinks drive more traffic to your website, increasing your visibility and potential customer base.
In essence, a well-executed backlink strategy not only improves your SEO but also establishes your site as a credible source of information, driving organic traffic and ultimately contributing to the growth and success of your online presence.
Here’s an example. When someone types “how to sell my house in [feature area]” or “real estate agent in [city]” into Google, you want your website to come up on the first page.
If your website does appear on the first page, you're tapping into significant website traffic, generating leads, and closing crucial deals. A staggering 93% of internet experiences start with a search engine, a trend that holds true in the real estate industry. When potential clients—your target market—are seeking assistance, they turn to Google.
Appearing on the first page of search results is paramount for business success.
Strategies for Building Backlinks
Building Backlinks with Local Citations
Getting listed in relevant directories is crucial for building your online presence and enhancing local SEO, not just for acquiring backlinks. Here’s why citations are essential and how to identify the best directories for your real estate business:
What are Citations?
Citations are online mentions of your real estate business that typically include your Name, Address, and Phone Number (NAP). These mentions can appear on various online platforms such as:
Local Business Directories:
Yelp, Google My Business, Bing Places for Business, etc.
Industry-Specific Directories:
Realtor.com, Zillow, Trulia, etc.
Local Government Websites:
City or county government websites often list licensed real estate agents.
Chamber of Commerce Listings:
Joining your local chamber can provide valuable directory listings.
Benefits of Citations for Real Estate Businesses:
Improved Local Search Ranking:
Search engines such as Google use consistent NAP citations (Name, Address, Phone Number) across various websites to verify the legitimacy and location of your business.
Consistent and accurate citations can significantly boost your website's ranking in local search results for relevant real estate keywords.
Increased Online Visibility:
Citations help potential clients discover your real estate business when they search for agents or properties online.
Listings on directories often include basic contact information, reviews, and sometimes links to your website, enhancing your visibility and directing more traffic to your site.
Backlink Potential:
Many reputable directories provide backlinks to your website along with your citation.
These backlinks contribute to your overall SEO efforts, improving your website's authority and potentially increasing its ranking in search engine results pages (SERPs).
Finding the Right Directories:
Focus on Relevance:
Don’t just submit your website to every directory you find. Prioritize directories relevant to your location, the real estate niche you serve, and those trusted by potential clients.
Local Directories First:
Start with local business directories and industry-specific real estate platforms.
Use Online Tools:
Several online tools like Moz Local or Yext can help you find high-quality directories and manage your citations across different platforms.
Maintaining Accuracy:
Once you’ve claimed your listings on relevant directories, ensure your NAP information is consistent across all platforms. Any inconsistencies can negatively impact your local SEO. Regularly monitor and update your listings as needed.
By building a strong citation profile through local directories, you establish your real estate business online, improve your local search rankings, and potentially earn valuable backlinks to your website. This comprehensive approach strengthens your online presence and attracts more qualified leads.
The Lofty SEO tab provides the tool to add and check online platform backlinks.
Learn more here:
Search Engine Optimization (SEO) Tool (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/21967062975515)
Link Building on Social Media
While social media links themselves do not directly impact SEO, the visibility and engagement they foster can lead to natural backlinks from various online sources.
Lofty's
Social Studio (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/4416954832795)
offers a powerful tool to promote your real estate content and attract backlinks.
Here’s how to maximize your efforts:
Identify Your Target Audience:
Platforms:
Not all social media platforms are created equal. Focus on platforms where your target audience spends their time (e.g., Facebook groups for local residents, LinkedIn for industry professionals).
Communities:
Join relevant Facebook groups, online forums, and subreddits focused on real estate in your area or niche.
Content Strategy for Backlinks:
Post Consistently:
Regularly share valuable content like listing posts, blog posts, local market updates, home buying tips, or visually appealing property listings.
Optimize for Sharing:
Include clear calls to action, encouraging viewers to share your content. Use relevant hashtags and engaging visuals to increase share ability.
Engage and Build Relationships:
Be a Valuable Contributor:
Don’t just post your content and disappear. Participate in discussions, answer questions, and offer helpful advice. Establish yourself as a trusted resource within the community.
Collaborate with Others:
Look for opportunities to collaborate with other real estate agents, lenders, or local businesses on social media campaigns. Cross-promotion can expand your reach and attract backlinks from their audience.
Consistent Content Creation
Produce detailed guides on local real estate trends and informative posts about market dynamics to attract backlinks from local news sites and community blogs.
Think of every piece of content like a door to your website. The more doors you have, the more people can visit your website, and the more opportunities you have to rank in Google. A good rule of thumb, though, is to create only one piece of content for each keyword phrase you’re targeting.
With the right strategies, your piece of content can become the show everyone’s talking about.
Informative Real Estate Guides
Informative guides are the map, making the journey easier and the destination clearer.
Easy-to-Digest:
Provide clear and concise guides that break down complex real estate topics.
Helpful Tips:
Include actionable advice for both new and seasoned property seekers or sellers.
Up-to-date:
Regularly update guides to reflect the current market trends and regulations.
Visual Content
Imagine diving into a property without even stepping in!
That’s the magic of visual content in the real estate industry.
It brings properties to life right on the screens of potential buyers.
Virtual Tours:
Give a 360-degree view of properties, letting viewers feel the space without a physical visit. You can create the perfect
virtual tour (https://rextheme.com/create-virtual-tour-complete-guide/)
with WPVR.
Engaging Imagery:
Use high-quality photos of properties, making them irresistible to viewers.
Infographics:
Break down real estate data into simple visual stories, making it easier to grasp.
Video Content:
Showcase properties with dynamic videos, offering viewers a cinematic experience of homes on sale.
Geo-targeted Content
Geo-targeted content in real estate is like having a local guide in a foreign city.
It offers insights specific to a location, ensuring your piece of content hits home—quite literally!
Local Market Reports:
Dive into specifics about a city, suburb, or even a street. What’s hot and what’s not?
Cultural Highlights:
Showcase local festivals, traditions, or events. Give a feel of the community spirit.
Area Profiles:
Detail amenities, schools, parks, and transport links in a particular region.
Property Spotlights:
Highlight properties in specific areas, giving potential buyers or renters a focused look.
Establishing Yourself as the Local Real Estate Expert: Building Trust and Backlinks
Becoming a local resource in the real estate market isn’t just about generating leads; it’s about building trust, establishing expertise, and attracting backlinks through valuable community engagement. By getting involved in community activities, you can increase your visibility and earn backlinks from event organizers and media outlets. Here are some strategic ways to position yourself as the go-to expert:
Offer Free Consultations and Resources:
Free Consultations:
Provide potential clients with free consultations to discuss their buying or selling needs. This allows you to showcase your knowledge, build rapport, and demonstrate your commitment to their success.
Host Educational Seminars:
Organize workshops or seminars on topics relevant to your target audience, such as “First-Time Homebuyer Tips” or “The Benefits of Selling Your Home in Today’s Market.” This establishes you as a thought leader and positions your website as a resource for valuable information.
Create Free Downloadable Resources:
Develop downloadable guides, checklists, or market reports that provide valuable insights for buyers and sellers. Make these resources freely available on your website with clear calls to action encouraging visitors to explore your services.
Participate in Local Events:
Industry Events:
Network with other professionals at real estate conferences, workshops, or association meetings. These events provide opportunities to build relationships, exchange knowledge, and potentially collaborate on future projects.
Community Events:
Actively participate in local community events like charity fundraisers, neighborhood clean-up initiatives, or local festivals. This demonstrates your commitment to the community and fosters positive brand recognition. Sponsor local events to gain further visibility and establish your brand as a trusted local partner.
Partner with Local Businesses:
Strategic Collaborations:
Partner with businesses that complement your real estate services, such as mortgage lenders, title companies, or home inspectors. Cross-promote each other’s services and leverage each other’s audience reach.
Local Publications:
Connect with local newspapers, online publications, or radio stations. Offer your expertise as a guest speaker or interviewee on topics related to the real estate market. This provides valuable exposure and potential backlinks when your website is mentioned as a resource.
Offer Free Content to Local Websites:
Contribute informative articles or blog posts to local publications or neighborhood websites. These guest posts establish you as an expert and can include backlinks to your website for further information.
Conclusion
Effective backlink building is a crucial, ongoing strategy for enhancing the digital presence and SEO of real estate websites. Each strategy outlined not only broadens the reach of your website but also solidifies its reputation and authority in the real estate industry.
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please contact our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

#### Article 436: Google Search Console: Understanding Index Coverage Issues

- Article ID: `26697006829595`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `SEO Best Practices`
- Updated: `2025-11-11T03:12:00Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/26697006829595-Google-Search-Console-Understanding-Index-Coverage-Issues

Introduction
Google Search Console (GSC) is a powerful tool that helps website owners monitor and maintain their website's presence in Google search results. One of the most crucial features is the Index Coverage Report, which identifies issues preventing pages from being indexed by Google.
This article explains the most common indexing issues reported by GCS and provides guidance on how to address them.
Understanding Common Index Issues
In most cases, you will not need to take any action. Many issues are related to problems on Google's end. These issues can be ignored while Google resolves them, generally within two weeks.
Issues that Google attributes to the website do not necessarily need to be corrected, as they are related to the website's indexing strategy. Please refer to the table below for details:
Issue
Explanation
Alternate page with proper canonical tag
This page is an alternate version (Accelerated Mobile Pages/AMP or mobile) of another indexed page and correctly points to the canonical version.
No action is needed. This issue arises from using canonical tags for AMP pages, which are designed for faster loading on mobile devices. Google does not index AMP pages separately, so this issue does not affect the overall website ranking.
Discovered - currently not indexed
The page was found by Google, but has not been crawled yet. Google wanted to crawl the URL, but this action was expected to overload the site. Therefore, Google rescheduled the crawl.
No action is necessary, but keep monitoring the trend.
Crawled - currently not indexed
The page was crawled by Google, but not indexed. It may or may not be indexed in the future. There is no need to resubmit the URL for crawling. This issue can occur for various reasons, and there is no specific operation that will make sure the page is indexed.
We recommend checking the page content and adding internal links to enhance the page's value for further indexing.
Excluded by 'no index' tag
The 'no index' tag is applied to pages that should not be indexed by search engines. In most cases, this exclusion is intentional to enhance the website's SEO effectiveness. These excluded pages are often unavailable property listings or pages with no search results.
No action is needed. The purpose of the exclusion is to instruct Google not to index these content-less pages, allowing it to prioritize and give more SEO weight to pages with valuable content.
Server error (5xx)
5xx errors can occasionally occur during periods of overload or maintenance, such as when Lofty releases feature updates or when web crawlers like Googlebot attempt to access the site too frequently. When this occurs, Google's crawler may not be able to retrieve content.
When this happens, Googlebot will attempt to to crawl the page again during its next visit. Additionally, Google keeps a record of pages that fail to load due to 5xx errors. This means that even after our servers stabilize, some pages may still show 5xx error until Google successfully crawls and indexes them.
No action is needed. These issues typically resolve themselves within 2-5 weeks as Google re-crawls affected pages. Lofty monitors these situations closely to avoid issue.
Page with redirect/Not Found (404)/Soft 404
When properties are taken off the market or if indexed pages are deleted in the CMS, different server responses may occur. These include pages that no longer exist, pages with no content, or pages that redirect elsewhere. As a result, you may see issues like Soft 404s, Not Found 404s, or pages with redirects in their reports.
In most cases, these issues do not require specific actions, as removing listings or deleting pages is a normal operation. Search engines like Google gradually update their indexes to recognize these changes and adjust accordingly.
Duplicate, Google chose a different canonical than the user
Canonical tags are HTML tags used to instruct search engines on the primary version of a page. We use this to specify which page should be indexed as the main content version. Google sometimes chooses a different canonical tag. This decision may be based on Google's algorithms determining a page with higher content quality or better user experience.
Generally, this does not significantly impact overall website ranking or SEO, as Google handles these conflicts appropriately.
Duplicate without a user-selected canonical
For highly similar pages, we've implemented canonical tags to specify the primary version. If you still see these issues in reports, it may be due to Google not yet updating its index.
If you need confirmation of the canonical tag settings for these pages, please contact
support@lofty.com (mailto:support@lofty.com)
for assistance.
Blocked by robots.txt
Lofty has blocked URLs in the format of "https://#domain#/house-listing..." using robots.txt, as these pages are intended for listing recommendation associations and hold no SEO value.
Please ignore this issue.
For more information, please see
Google's Page Indexing Report (https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7440203?hl=en)
Conclusion
We advise that you not overly fixate on the reasons for individual pages not being indexed. Instead, we recommend focusing on the broader trends of the indexed pages. You should find that as the number of pages discovered by search engines rises steadily, the count of indexed pages is also gradually increasing.
We are dedicated to continuously enhancing your website's SEO. Here are some recent optimizations we have made:
SEO Updates Timeline (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/14489319973531)
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

Setup and Initial Optimization

.

Content Generation and Management
Blog Editors
Lofty's blog editor is designed to enhance your real estate IDX website by providing tools for creating, categorizing, and styling blog posts. It includes advanced options for SEO and content scheduling, allowing for a dynamic approach to content management. The editor supports various content types such as text, images, videos, and even embedded source code, making it versatile for different kinds of posts. You can customize meta titles, descriptions, and keywords for each post, which is essential for optimizing search engine visibility. Blog Page (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360039336851)
Adding Featured Area Pages
Navigate to your website and click the
Areas
tab. Click the blue button +Add New Area/Neighborhood to add the cities and neighborhoods where you specialize.
Lofty's CMS provides a range of page templates, including ones specifically designed for adding featured areas on your website. These templates allow real estate agents to showcase specific neighborhoods or regions, enhancing the user experience and focusing on areas of interest. Engaging with Listings Videos

, enhancing how real estate professionals can market properties. Select up to six (6) images from the listing to create a video. These videos can be customized with different templates and aspect ratios to optimize visibility across various social media platforms.
Lofty offers this capability directly from the Social Studio, which also allows you to schedule and manage posts. This feature is particularly valuable for engaging potential clients and increasing the visibility of listings online.
Collecting and Displaying Reviews

For more detailed instructions and settings related to managing and displaying reviews on Lofty, including step-by-step guides on integrating reviews from Zillow, Google, and RateMyAgent, please refer to our Help Center articles here:
Reviews Block (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360038293251)
and

Sharing Content Regularly

Social Studio offers comprehensive tools to streamline this process. Here's how it helps you manage and share your content consistently.
Content Scheduling and Management:
Social Studio allows you to plan and schedule your social media posts in advance. This ensures that your content is distributed evenly over time, keeping your audience engaged without overwhelming them with too many updates at once. You can create a content calendar that outlines what and when to post, making it easier to manage your social media strategy systematically.
Post Creation and Customization:
The platform provides a robust editor to create and customize your posts. You can include various types of media, such as images, videos, and links, to enhance the appeal of your posts. The editor supports different styles and formats, allowing you to tailor each post to suit the specific platform you are targeting.

Link Building and Social Proof
Social Backlinks Generation
High-quality backlinks from reputable sites and social media platforms significantly enhance your domain authority. Engage with your community on social media, share valuable content, and participate in local events to build a robust backlink profile. Backlinks signal to search engines that your content is valuable and trustworthy, which can improve your rankings.
The Social Agent features are designed to seamlessly integrate your real estate website with various social platforms, facilitating efficient backlink generation. By connecting your Lofty account to your social media profiles, you can effortlessly share you content across multiple channels. This not only drives traffic to your site but also boosts your SEO through increased backlinks. The platform supports integration with major social networks, enabling automatic posting of new content and updates. This integration ensures that your audience on platforms like Facebook, Twitter, and LinkedIn stays informed and engaged, while also enhancing your site's visibility and credibility through consistent social signals.
Performance and Monitoring
Conducting Site Audits
Built-in audit tools:
Conducting regular site audits is essential to maintaining a healthy and optimized website. Lofty's platform simplifies this process by offering built-in audit tools that analyze various aspects of your site, including page speed, mobile responsiveness, and SEO elements. These audits help identify areas that need improvement, such as broken links, missing meta descriptions, or slow-loading pages. Addressing these issues promptly can significantly enhance your site's performance and search engine visibility. Learn more about Lofty's SEO tools here:

Optimizing on-page elements:
On-page optimization is a crucial aspect of SEO that involves fine-tuning individual pages to rank higher and earn more relevant traffic in search engines. Lofty provides an easy to use interface for optimizing key on-page elements such as titles, meta descriptions, headers, and image alt texts. By ensuring that each page is optimized with relevant keywords and compelling content, you can improve your site's SEO and provide a better user experience.
Technical Page Speed Improvements
Page speed is a vital factor in both user experience and SEO. Slow-loading pages can lead to higher bounce rates and lower search rankings. Test your website page speed here:

#### Article 438: Minimize SEO Setbacks when Changing your Site Domain

- Article ID: `32089405166363`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `SEO Best Practices`
- Updated: `2025-11-11T03:02:21Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/32089405166363-Minimize-SEO-Setbacks-when-Changing-your-Site-Domain

Introduction
If you've change your website's domain, it's important to notify Google Search Console to ensure that your site's performance, indexing, and SEO are properly tracked under the new domain. Follow these steps to update your website's domain in Google Search Console:
Step 1: Verify Ownership of the New Domain
Before making any changes in Google Search Console, make sure you've verified ownership of your new domain.
Log in to Google Search Console:
Go to Google Search Console and log in with your Google account.
Add Property for the New Domain:
Click on the "Add Property" button in the top-left corner.
Enter the URL of your new domain (including the
https://
) and follow the verification steps provided by Google.
Step 2: Set Up a Domain Change Request
Google provides a special tool called
Change of Address
to inform Google of your website domain change.
Navigate to the Old Domain's Property:
In Google Search Console, select the property for your old domain.
Go to the Settings:
Click on the "Settings" option in the left sidebar.
Under "Property Settings," select the "Change of Address" option.
Follow the Change of Address Wizard:
Google will ask you to select the new domain that you've verified in Google Search Console.
Choose the correct new domain from the list of verified properties.
Google will walk you through confirming that the domain move is permanent and that you've set up proper redirects on your old site.
Step 3: Implement 301 Redirects
Ensure that you've set up
301 redirects
on your old website domain to direct all traffic (and search engine crawlers) to the corresponding pages on your new domain. This is essential for transferring SEO value to the new domain.
Set Up 301 Redirects on your Old Domain:
Implement 301 redirects for each page of your old domain to the equivalent page on the new domain.
If you're using a CMS like WordPress, there are plugins that can help with this process.
Note:
301 redirects tell Google that the page has permanently moved to a new location, helping preserve your SEO rankings.
Step 4: Update Sitemaps in Google Search Console
After your domain change, update your sitemaps to reflect the new URLs.
Submit a New Sitemap for the New Domain
In Google Search Console, go to the property for your new domain.
Under the "Sitemaps" section, click "Add/Text Sitemap" and submit the updated sitemap for your new domain.
Make sure that the sitemap includes URLs of the new domain and reflects all the pages that should be indexed.
Step 5: Monitor the Transition
Once the domain change is complete, monitor your site's performance and indexing to ensure everything is working correctly.
Check Coverage Reports:
In the "Coverage" section of Google Search Console, keep an eye on any errors related to indexing or redirect issues.
Track Traffic:
Use the "Performance" section to monitor how search traffic is evolving on your new domain.
Check for Crawling Errors:
Regularly check for crawling errors in the "Crawl Errors" section to ensure that Google is able to access your pages without issues.
Step 6: Update External Links
If possible, reach out to websites that link to your old domain and request that they update their links to your new domain. This helps to maintain link equity and improve your SEO performance.
Additional Tips
Update Google Analytics
Make sure that your Google Analytics account reflects the new domain for accurate tracking.
Notify Social Media and Marketing Channels
Update your domain on all external platforms like social media profiles, email newsletters, and marketing materials.
By following these steps, you'll ensure that your website's SEO performance and indexing are properly maintained after changing domains. Google Search Console will help you manage the transition, but remember to monitor the results and fix any potential issues that arise during the process.
Questions?

#### Article 439: Navigating Common SEO Pitfalls in Real Estate

- Article ID: `27854660233883`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `SEO Best Practices`
- Updated: `2025-11-11T03:11:39Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/27854660233883-Navigating-Common-SEO-Pitfalls-in-Real-Estate

Introduction
This article delves into common SEO challenges faced by real estate professionals and provides practical advice on enhancing online visibility effectively, drawing on successful industry practices.
Summary
High-Difficulty and Overused Keywords (#h_01J42W3PFA3YRS55J0BH1ZKGGE)
Keyword Stuffing (#h_01J42W67HKA2YSCVXEVDZ38S45)
Missing Meta Descriptions and Title Tags (#h_01J42W8GSKTB0Q2KB35NSTQHRA)
Not Utilizing Social Media (#h_01J42W91X7W84K81HWJN2BYFW9)
Inconsistent NAP Information (#h_01J42WAZMCM9VNXHP4J0CM5MF5)
Duplicate Content (#h_01J42WBRY0Q7QH7RRKDQ1Q092J)
High-Difficulty and Overused Keywords
In real estate, highly competitive keywords like "real estate", "MLS", "realtor", or "luxury homes" are difficult to rank for due to their broad appeal. For instance, a small agency trying to compete for these terms might find itself overshadowed by larger, national companies. A more effective strategy is to focus on
local
and
long-tail
keywords that have less competition and higher conversion rates, such as "eco-friendly condos in Boulder" or "historic homes for sale in Savannah." These keywords are not only easier to rank for but also attract a more targeted audience.
Keyword Stuffing
The practice of keyword stuffing can severely impact the user experience and diminish a website's credibility. For example, a webpage overly saturated with the phrase "affordable Miami apartments" can become difficult to read and may be penalized by search engines, leading to lower rankings. Instead, it is recommended to integrate keywords naturally into the content, ensuring it remains informative and engaging. This approach aligns with Google’s emphasis on content quality, which rewards websites that provide value to their users.
Missing Meta Descriptions and Title Tags
Often overlooked, meta descriptions and title tags are essential for improving click-through rates from SERPs. For example, a well-crafted title tag and meta description for a listing page could be "Modern Seattle Waterfront Homes | Browse Listings and Tours," with a compelling description that outlines what to expect on the page. Ignoring these elements can result in missed opportunities to capture interest at the crucial moment when potential clients are deciding which link to click on in their search results.
Not Utilizing Social Media
Ignoring the power of social media can limit a real estate agency’s ability to reach a broader audience. For instance, sharing a post about a new property listing on platforms like Instagram and Facebook can lead to increased engagement and website traffic. Moreover, real estate professionals who actively engage with their followers through comments and shares typically build a stronger online presence, which indirectly supports SEO through increased brand visibility and the generation of organic backlinks.
Lofty providesa  powerful social management tool to keep your site alive on social media and gain engagement with automatic social posts.
Learn more about Social Studio:
Social Studio (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/4416954832795)
Inconsistent NAP Information
NAP (Name, Address, Phone Number) inconsistencies across the internet can confuse both users and search engines, potentially harming local SEO efforts. For instance, if a real estate company’s Google My Business profile has a different phone number than its website, it might reduce the business's credibility and search engine ranking. Ensuring consistency in NAP information across all platforms is crucial for boosting local search visibility.
Duplicate Content
Real estate websites often inadvertently feature duplicate content, such as similar listings posted across multiple pages or websites. This can dilute the website's SEO value, as search engines might struggle to determine which content to prioritize. For example, two property listings described in nearly identical language but posted in separate sections can compete against each other in search rankings. Using unique, original content for each listing enhances SEO by clearly distinguishing each page as unique and relevant.
Conclusion
Understanding and addressing these SEO pitfalls with strategic adjustments can significantly enhance a real estate website's search engine visibility and user engagement. By focusing on tailored keyword strategies, refining meta tags, leveraging social media, ensuring data consistency, and maintaining unique content, real estate professionals can drive more targeted traffic and generate valuable leads effectively. For more detailed strategies and examples,
How Lofty Supports SEO (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/27072683872667)
offers further insights and recommendations tailored to real estate marketing.
Questions?

#### Article 440: Edit Website Meta Tags

- Article ID: `360038183991`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `SEO Tool`
- Updated: `2025-11-11T03:17:19Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360038183991-Edit-Website-Meta-Tags

Introduction
Meta tags are snippets of text that describe a page’s content. The meta tags do not appear on the page itself, only in the page’s source code. Meta tags can help Google and other search engines understand your content and thus help your SEO ranking if adjusted correctly.
Lofty supports the ability to configure the
meta title
,
meta keywords
, and
meta description
for each page.
Summary
Meta Title (#h_01GYFRV5MEFK8BJS5FQ5V8T0JK)
Meta Description (#h_01GYFRVAYFQ3W4C6A7S7YKZRZA)
Meta Keywords (#h_01GYFRVK799EASNXT0XG2K0H4A)
Editing Meta Tags (#h_01GYFRVSGVS0B5E81MCYDGS3YW)
Meta Title
This is the text you will see at the top of your browser. Search engines view this text as the "title" of your page. These tags have a real impact on search rankings and allow visitors to easily distinguish your site from others.
Meta Description
Meta Description is a brief description of the page and, put simply, explains to search engines and (sometimes) searchers themselves what your page is about. Please note that the meta description tag will not always show up in the results of a Google search.
Meta Keywords
Meta Keywords are a series of keywords you deem relevant to the page in question. Nowadays, they are not as useful as they once were. They no longer provide any real benefit for SEO.
Even though Lofty
supports the ability to configure meta keywords, we do not recommend that you configure them.
Editing Meta Tags
First of all, find the page that you want to edit on your CMS Tool navigation and then click on the "Edit" icon:
From this section, you can configure the "Page SEO" which includes the meta title, meta keywords, and meta description of the page. This also supports the insertion of variables (merge fields) that will update automatically with adjustments via the CMS Tool.
The "SNS Cover Photo" is the social media cover photo of this page. This image is also used when sharing this page in iMessage or email.
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

#### Article 443: SEO Optimization and Google Search Console Integration

- Article ID: `26400494235035`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `SEO Tool`
- Updated: `2025-11-11T03:16:02Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/26400494235035-SEO-Optimization-and-Google-Search-Console-Integration

Introduction
Lofty is performing SEO optimization for all active Company, Team, and Agent websites. This process involves monitoring the indexing status of these websites using
Google Search Console (GSC) (https://search.google.com/search-console/about)
.
GSC allows Lofty to monitor your website's indexing status and provide data support for SEO optimization. Please be assured that Lofty will not make any unauthorized changes to your website and we do not have ownership of your website domain. Integrating your website with Lofty's Google Search Console account is a crucial step in enhancing your website's SEO performance.
Summary
Adding Your Site to Google Search Console (#h_01HZSM864XDAVEG9Z6J724KEGB)
Purpose and Benefits (#h_01HZSMF3JJTW6B9FTRZVDQ27VW)
Control and Permissions (#h_01HZSMRBT5PR1EKP05VBR2XK00)
Adding Your Site to Google Search Console
To effectively track and optimize your website's performance, Lofty will need to add your website to our public Google Search Console account. Once your site has been added, you will receive an email notification with the subject line
New Owner Notice
, that is letting you know that an email address with the format
siteanalytics#number#@lofty.com
has been added as an owner of your website in GSC. Please see an example of this email below:
Purpose and Benefits
The primary goal of the GSC integration is overall SEO optimization. While immediate benefits may not be noticeable, having owner permissions allows Lofty to use the official GSC API to gain insights into your website's ranking and indexing status. Here are the key advantages:
Issue Resolution:
Lofty will prioritize fixing issues for websites with no traffic first, followed by optimizing overall traffic.
Monitoring and Insights:
Regular insights into your website's performance will help us identify and resolve indexing issues.
Prompt Assistance:
If you have already verified ownership in GSC, you may receive periodic emails about indexing issues. With access to your GSC account, Lofty can quickly assist in resolving or explaining these issues.
Control and Permissions
Lofty respects your control over your website. We will not make any changes to your website without your permission. If you prefer not to have Lofty has the owner of your website on Google Search Console, simply follow these steps to remove our account (siteanalytics#number#@lofty.com) from your GSC settings.
Log in to your Google Search Console account
Select your website
Navigate to the
Settings
section
Under
Users and Permissions
, locate Lofty's account: siteanalytics#number#@lofty.com
Remove the account by clicking the remove icon
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

#### Article 445: Website SEO (Search Engine Optimization)

- Article ID: `360039873672`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `SEO Tool`
- Updated: `2025-11-11T03:18:03Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360039873672-Website-SEO-Search-Engine-Optimization

Introduction
SEO stands for “search engine optimization.” It is the process of getting traffic from the “free,” “organic,” “editorial,” or “natural” search results on search engines.
Your Lofty site has been built using SEO best practices, but there are things that you can be doing to help increase site validity and reputation in the eyes of Google. Remember, SEO is a marathon, not a sprint! You must be consistent with your efforts over long periods for SEO to be improved and harnessed as a tool. SEO is about building your relationship with search engines as a valuable and reliable website and resource.
Summary
This article will review a few important ways you can begin your SEO journey with Lofty websites.
Add Unique Meta Data to Every Page on Your Website (#h_01EF2DKE8YAAFYGHZ5CB4SZ4YY)
Start Relevant and Regular Blogging (#h_01EF2DKJJDM8K7QQRJABBG45PK)
Add Reviews to your Website (#h_01FGSPX54Q75394ABDQPBGWM7T)
Increase Backlinking to Your Site (#h_01EF2DKPTTCHCFCQR940X86CAP)
Additional Resources (#h_01EF2DKWME48DGX46XQPPQ7QT5)
301 Redirects (#h_01EF2EJBDNE0D4GYCGYSQCJ1ZY)
Image and Content Hosting (#h_01F8TT10Y6B1FVG94ZAMMF6WQW)
Add Unique Meta Data to Every Page on Your Website
A "meta description" is a snippet of up to about 155 characters – a tag in HTML – which summarizes a page's content. Search engines show the meta description in search results mostly when the searched-for phrase is within the description, so optimizing the meta descriptions is crucial.
Best Practices
Add an accurate name for each page
Create separate pages for different products, services, and topics
Stay between
50 and 160 characters
for your Meta Page Descriptions
Stay under 60 characters for your Meta Page Titles
Put important keywords first
Do not overdo SEO keywords. While there is no penalty built into Google's algorithm for long titles, you can run into trouble if you start stuffing your title full of keywords in a way that creates a bad user experience
Give every page a unique title. Unique titles help search engines understand that your content is unique and valuable, and also drive higher click-through rates
Write for your customers. While title tags are very important to SEO, remember that your first job is attracting clicks from well-targeted visitors who will likely find your content valuable.
Add an appropriate cover image that relates to your content
Put the most important information
in writing
. Using rich content, including videos, audio clips, animations, etc., can help to maintain the attention of your site visitors for a longer period,
but
search engines do not understand videos, audio, etc. So, use text for important information as much as possible.
Make sure to add alt text with your site's name for your logo on your website. It would also be a good idea to include your website's name in the text somewhere else on that page.
Add heading tags. The H1 tag (a.k.a "heading tag") serves as the title for each page. This tag should be like the headline of a page, just like you have a headline on a page within the newspaper, etc. At Lofty, we have already populated the H1 to H5 tags for each page for you.
How to Use Lofty CMS to Make Changes
To make changes to existing pages in Lofty using the New CMS, do the following:
To edit the logo and alt text, please reference the
Header (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360054747512)
.
Start Relevant and Regular Blogging
Blogging, when done regularly and with relevant information, can help boost your SEO rankings. There are many ways you can use blogging as a Real Estate Agent.
You can use blogging to help establish yourself as an area expert, provide helpful information to future residents, or help educate your Buyers and Sellers on buying and selling in today's market. People investigate the areas they are moving to and want to understand what there is to do in the area, where the best places to eat might be, or how walkable the area is.
You can even use blogging to help increase Backlinking, which is explained more in-depth in the following section. For example, if you learn about an amazing restaurant in the area, blog about it and let that restaurant know. Chances are, they will use your link and post it to their social media or site to let their audience know they were featured. This is one way to increase your Backlinking.
To learn how to use Lofty to blog, please reference the following article:
Blog Page (https://help.chime.me/hc/en-us/articles/360039336851)
.
Add Reviews to Your Website
One thing that site visitors will expect to see on your website is reviews of your services and organization. You will want to do your best to meet that expectation by adding reviews to different pages on your website. Learn more about how to do this with the following articles:
Reviews Page (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360038133432)
Reviews Block (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360038293251)
Increase Backlinking to Your Site
Backlinks are when you are listed on another site and are especially valuable for SEO. They represent a "vote of confidence" from one site to another. In essence, backlinks to your website are a signal to search engines that others vouch for your content. If many sites link to the same webpage or website, search engines can infer that the content is worth linking to, and therefore also worth surfacing on a search engine results page. So, earning these backlinks can have a positive effect on a site's ranking position or search visibility.
Add backlinks to your website on your social media pages, and other real estate websites where you have a profile (Trulia, Realtor.com, brand websites, etc.).
How many sites are currently backlinking to your site, and what can you do to increase that number?
Additional Resources
Below are a couple of additional resources to keep in your back pocket. They were created to help you understand the basics of SEO and how it relates to Lofty.
SEO for Real Estate Webinar Series (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T2lffbSEeLM&list=PLpFx04vC9Ecvnxwf-JUR-m6pJEqj9pYaC)
301 Redirects
Setting up 301 redirects is like forwarding your mail after a move. If you are migrating from an old website to a Lofty website, you might have heard about 301 redirects and have a few questions about how they work at Lofty. For all inquiries in this area, please submit a request via your Onboarding Specialist, Customer Success Manager (CSM), or our Support Team (
support@lofty.com (mailto:support@chimeinc.com)
) for additional assistance.
Please note that all 301 redirects have to be done manually. Because of this, Lofty is
not
able
to do this on an individual, page-by-page basis. If you have pages that you want to be redirected, a request can be submitted to redirect
multiple
pages to
one
page on Lofty. In most scenarios, redirecting to your Lofty IDX website home page is sufficient, as it keeps site visitors from getting lost.
If you are bringing over your domain to Lofty, you can also work on recreating the same pages on Lofty. This can work, but it will depend on the page structure that you are trying to create.
If you are concerned about how a large number of "dead links" will affect your SEO, Lofty can help to submit a request to Google to help remove the dead links to avoid potential problems here.
Image and Content Hosting
Though not specifically "SEO," page load time is extremely important for your site's reputation. One question that has been asked before is how images are hosted on Lofty websites. The answer is that this is done via CDN (Content Delivery Network), which improves load speed overall.
To learn more about CDN, see
What is a CDN? | How do CDNs work (https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/cdn/what-is-a-cdn/)
?
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your Lofty CRM.
Related terms: SEO, search engine, indexing, meta, meta tags, site header, page load time

### Section: SSL

#### Article 446: Website SSL Certificates

- Article ID: `360004842792`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `SSL`
- Updated: `2025-11-11T06:29:56Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360004842792-Website-SSL-Certificates

Introduction
An SSL certificate can help keep your site secure to ensure that it is trusted by the browsers and operating systems of your website visitors. You can purchase an SSL certificate via your domain provider or a third party, and Lofty can help you have it installed on your website.
Installing an SSL certificate is important for the following reasons:
Facebook regulations will not allow for unsecured sites to be shared on their platform. Also, without an SSL, the option to "Log in with Facebook" cannot be used on your Lofty website.
Some specific internet browsers will often force a URL typed into the search bar to go to the "https://" which means that a secure site with the SSL certificate is expected.
Here are a few screenshots to demonstrate the error that might appear when navigating to a site that does not have an SSL Certificate installed:
Not Required by Lofty
As a note, this is not required by Lofty to use the service. But, it is something that will benefit people browsing your website. If you so desired, you could click on the "ADVANCED" option seen in the bottom-left of the last screenshot, and choose to continue to the website. This would allow your browser to trust the Lofty site. However, this is not acceptable to many who will visit your website and could deter them from using your site.
Any site under a Lofty domain, such as ________.lofty.com, is always secure because we have already installed a wildcard SSL certification for all these sites automatically. You will only need to plan on having a separate SSL certificate installed if you plan to configure your domain to be different from the provided _________.lofty.com domain.
SSL Certificate Setup
(1) Did you purchase your domain via Lofty?
If you purchased your domain via Lofty (see
Vanity Domain Purchase (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/4403710715547)
) then an SSL certificate will be installed on your purchased website automatically and does not require configuration.
(2) Do you have an SSL Certificate already?
Please send us the information below to <support@lofty.com> so that we can generate a
CSR file
for your SSL certificate:
Country Name
State or Province Name (complete name)
Locality Name (Example: city)
Organization Name (Example: company)
Organizational Unit Name (Example: section)
Common Name (Example: your name or your server host's name)
Email Address
After Lofty Support receives the above information, the quickest route is to also provide Lofty Support with the login credentials (login URL, username, email, and password) for your SSL Provider so that configuration can be finalized.
However, if you are not comfortable with sending your SSL Provider credentials, please follow these steps:
Upload the CSR file (now generated by Lofty) to your SSL Certificate
Download the certificate file in Apache format
Send the certificate file to <support@lofty.com>
After these steps are complete, the SSL Certification should be installed on your domain.
(3) Do you
not
have an SSL Certificate already?
Lofty offers a free SSL Certificate that can be used to keep your site secure.
After completing the domain configuration
(see
Domain Configuration Guide (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360054554712)
), please send an email to <support@lofty.com> to arrange for the SSL to be installed.
Please note that if you have many subdomain websites, you will need a wildcard SSL certificate installed, and, depending on the situation, this might require purchasing on your end as it might not be available with the service used by Lofty. Please contact our Support Team to see what can be done in this scenario.
Additional Information
If you would like more information regarding the topic of SSL Certificates, please feel free to research the topic further with any domain provider as well as many online resources. Additional information can also be found in this
Beginner’s Guide to SSL Certificates (https://www.digicert.com/resources/beginners-guide-to-tls-ssl-certificates-whitepaper-en-2019.pdf)
as written by Symantec Corporation.
HostGator published this article related to the topic as well:
What the July Google Chrome Update Means for Your Website (https://www.hostgator.com/blog/2018-google-chrome-update/?utm_campaign=email&utm_medium=not&utm_source=HGfreessl-email%201&utm_content=)
FAQ
Q: Should I call to renew my SSL with Lofty?
A: SSL certificates are set to auto-renew every 90 days. In case of issues, please reach out to our Support Team for immediate assistance.
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

#### Article 447: Changing the Website Theme

- Article ID: `360037814232`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `Theme Color & Font`
- Updated: `2025-11-11T09:18:38Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360037814232-Changing-the-Website-Theme

Introduction
The website theme is one of the first things someone will notice about your site so it's important to get it right. You will want to choose colors that compliment your logo, brand, and overall appearance.
Edit the Theme
Start by clicking "Style" in the Page Editor:
Under the "Theme" menu, you can edit the theme color, title style, and button style.
Theme Color
This consists of two parts: (1) primary color and (2) hover color. This applies to all colors except the title and buttons. The "Primary Color" is the default color for most elements on a website. The "Hover Color" is the hover color of all clickable elements on the website.
Title Style
Used to edit the title style of all blocks.
Button Style
To edit the style of all buttons.
Preview Changes
After modifying the website theme, you will immediately see the website style change in the preview pane on the right. You can switch pages to see the effect of different pages and adjust some block styles to make the website look better.
If you want to go back to the previous style, click the "Undo" icon on the top bar.
To save any changes, be sure to hit the "Publish" button in the top-right for this to apply to the live website.
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by a chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

- Article ID: `360038610171`

Introduction
In the CMS Tool, you can edit the settings associated with the chat box on your website. This is a good way to engage site visitors.
*IMPORTANT
: If the
AI Assistant (https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/360056322172)
is enabled, the chat box will
not
appear on your website as the AI Assistant's efforts to engage site visitors take priority.
Summary
Edit Chat Box Settings (#h_d75ddb20-6e07-4a85-957b-5ff7d1494c2b)
Facebook Messenger (#h_b481f877-c06f-4efe-97fe-cdd33e459dd6)
Live Chat Explanation (#h_01F8TFG5HYF67XKQK69X61Y9PP)
Edit Chat Box Settings
To edit the chat box, open the CMS Tool > Settings > Lead Capture > Chat Box Settings:
The first setting to edit is whether to display the chat box. Users who choose not to display the chat box might do so to limit the number of available channels on their website to avoid any confusion, or they might want to embed a third-party chat box of some sort (which may require customization and associated customization fees). See
below (https://help.chime.me/hc/en-us/articles/360038610171#h_b481f877-c06f-4efe-97fe-cdd33e459dd6)
for Facebook Messenger support.
Enabling this setting will display the chat box. Disabling will keep the chat box from appearing on the website at all.
Here, you can decide whether to show the Company or the Agent as the Chat Agent. If you choose "Company", the Chat Box leads will be company leads.
If you choose "Agent", next select the agent from the available list.
Decide whether to display agent information or company information on the chat box.
Next, choose the "Agent Image Style," which is simply the shape of the image in the bottom-right:

he lead will also receive that message on their cell phone (if compatible) if they provide it during registration.

#### Article 450: Cancel, Reset, or Downgrade Website

- Article ID: `26507515965339`
- Category: `Website`
- Section: `Website Creation`
- Updated: `2025-11-11T02:37:41Z`
- URL: https://help.lofty.com/hc/en-us/articles/26507515965339-Cancel-Reset-or-Downgrade-Website

Introduction
Lofty offers many types of IDX websites, each having its own settings and abilities. This article explains how to cancel, reset, or downgrade your Lofty-built website.
Definitions
Reset:
Resetting the website will remove all customized content and revert the website to the blank template.
Downgrade:
Downgrading the website will revert the website to a subdomain of another website.
Cancel:
Cancelling the website will cancel the entire website package and delete the website, as well as any subdomains built off of this website.
Requirements and Limitations
While all Lofty-built websites can be reset, there is a limitation on what websites can be downgraded or canceled. Please take a look at the chart below to figure out which actions can be taken on your website. If you aren't sure what kind of website you have, you can just go to the
Website
tab in the CRM and check the
Type
column.
Website Type
Can it be reset?
Can it be downgraded?
Can it be cancelled?
Company Website + Full SEO
Yes
No
No
Team Website + Full SEO
Yes
No
Yes
Office Website + Full SEO
Yes
No
Yes
Agent Website + Full SEO
Yes
Yes
Yes
Agent Website (Original)
Yes
Yes
No
Agent Website
Yes
No
No
Websites can only be downgraded if their parent site has a vanity domain. If the parent site domain has not been configured, the website cannot be downgraded.
At this time, only Office Website + SEO and Agent website + SEO can be canceled. Once the website is canceled, the website and any subdomains built off of the website will be deleted.
Instructions
Navigate to
Website
and select the website that you want to take action on. You are only able to reset, downgrade, or cancel websites that you are paying for. You cannot take these actions on a website that is paid for by another Lofty user.
Click the
...
icon to see the available options.
Once the action is selected, a pop-up box will confirm that you wish to continue. To complete the action, a verification code will be sent to the email address associated with the website owner. The code must be verified to complete the action.
When canceling a website, you can opt to cancel now or cancel at the end of the month.
A final confirmation will verify that the action will take place. Once complete, the action is irreversible.
If a website is canceled, reset, or downgraded, Lofty cannot undo this action.
Questions?
If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your Lofty CRM.
